lessons.title: Community Service Should Be Encouraged, Not Used as Punishment
lessons.topic: Community Service Should Be Encouraged, Not Used as Punishment
lessons.passage: Community service is supposed to help people understand responsibility and contribute to others. When it is used mainly as punishment, students may begin to see helping the community as something negative. I would rather schools encourage service through meaningful projects connected to real needs. Some programmes can still be expected as part of school education, but students should understand the purpose and be treated respectfully. Consequences for poor behaviour may be necessary, yet they can take other forms. Volunteering works best when young people see the value of the activity itself, not when they are waiting for the punishment to end.

lessons.title: Popularity Is Not a Good Measure of Success
lessons.topic: Popularity Is Not a Good Measure of Success
lessons.passage: At school and online, popular people can appear to have the most successful social lives. But popularity often depends on attention, trends or being known by many people, none of which tells us whether someone is happy, kind or confident. A quieter student may have strong friendships and feel comfortable with who they are. Being liked is pleasant, and there is nothing wrong with enjoying social attention. The problem is using popularity as a measure of self-worth. Success in relationships is better measured by trust, respect and genuine connection than by how many people know your name.

lessons.title: School Prizes Should Recognise Improvement as Well as Achievement
lessons.topic: School Prizes Should Recognise Improvement as Well as Achievement
lessons.passage: Students who achieve excellent results deserve recognition, but achievement is not the only success worth noticing. A student who moves from struggling to making steady progress may have worked extremely hard even if they are not at the top of the class. Schools can recognise improvement, effort, teamwork or service alongside high academic results. This does not mean giving everyone a prize for ordinary participation. Awards should still mean something. Broadening what schools celebrate sends a healthier message: excellence matters, but growth matters too. Students should be able to see more than one path to doing something worth being proud of.

lessons.title: Competition Is Useful Only When It Is Healthy
lessons.topic: Competition Is Useful Only When It Is Healthy
lessons.passage: Competition can give people a reason to practise harder and see how their skills compare with others. It can also make games, debates and school events exciting. The benefits disappear when winning becomes so important that students cheat, insult others or feel worthless after losing. Healthy competition needs fair rules, sportsmanship and respect for effort. Students should be able to challenge one another without turning every activity into a judgement of personal value. Competition is useful when it pushes people to improve while keeping the experience enjoyable. When pressure becomes the main feeling, the competition has stopped serving its purpose.

The benefits disappear when winning becomes so important that students cheat, insult others or feel worthless after losing.
Healthy competition needs fair rules, sportsmanship and respect for effort.
Students should be able to challenge one another without turning every activity into a judgement of personal value.
Competition is useful when it pushes people to improve while keeping the experience enjoyable.
When pressure becomes the main feeling, the competition has stopped serving its purpose.

lessons.title: Food Waste Should Be Reduced Before Food Choices Are Restricted
lessons.topic: Food Waste Should Be Reduced Before Food Choices Are Restricted
lessons.passage: When people discuss food and the environment, they sometimes begin by telling everyone what they should stop eating. I think reducing waste is a better first step because almost every family and school can improve it. Taking sensible portions, storing safe leftovers and planning meals carefully can prevent good food from reaching the bin. Food choices are connected to culture, health and personal needs, so strict restrictions can become complicated. Waste reduction is not the only environmental solution, but it is practical and widely useful. Before arguing about what should disappear from the menu, we should make better use of the food we already produce.

lessons.title: Schools Should Have Meat-Free Meal Options
lessons.topic: Schools Should Have Meat-Free Meal Options
lessons.passage: School canteens serve students with different tastes, family habits and dietary needs. Offering at least one meat-free option gives students more choice and can introduce meals based on beans, tofu, eggs or other ingredients. The option should still be balanced and nutritious; removing meat does not automatically make a meal healthy. I do not think every student should be forced to choose it or that schools need to remove meat completely. The key word is option. A varied menu is better than a one-size-fits-all approach because students can learn that healthy meals can be prepared in more than one way.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn More About Climate Change Solutions
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn More About Climate Change Solutions
lessons.passage: Students often hear about the problems caused by climate change, but learning only about danger can make the topic feel hopeless. Schools should also teach the range of solutions being tried, from cleaner energy and public transport to protecting forests and adapting cities to extreme weather. Students should examine evidence and understand that no single solution fixes everything. They also need to distinguish between actions individuals can take and changes that require businesses or governments. Solution-focused learning is more useful because it combines scientific understanding with practical thinking. Young people should leave the topic informed and realistic, not simply frightened.

lessons.title: Keeping Wild Animals as Pets Should Be Restricted
lessons.topic: Keeping Wild Animals as Pets Should Be Restricted
lessons.passage: Some wild animals look interesting or beautiful, but that does not mean they belong in ordinary homes. Exotic species may need special food, large spaces or environmental conditions that owners cannot provide. They can also become dangerous as they grow, and the pet trade can harm wild populations. There may be licensed experts or rescue centres with the knowledge to care for certain animals properly. That is different from keeping a wild species simply because it seems unusual. Ownership should be restricted when animal welfare, public safety or conservation is at risk. Wanting an animal is not enough; we must be able to meet its real needs.

lessons.title: Zoos Should Be Judged by Animal Welfare, Not Entertainment
lessons.topic: Zoos Should Be Judged by Animal Welfare, Not Entertainment
lessons.passage: A zoo should not be considered good simply because visitors enjoy seeing unusual animals. The first question should be whether the animals have proper care, suitable space and conditions that support their welfare. Good zoos may also contribute to conservation, education and research. Poor facilities that keep animals mainly for entertainment are much harder to defend. It can be difficult for visitors to judge every detail, so independent standards and professional care are important. I think the debate about zoos should focus less on whether people have fun and more on whether the institution genuinely protects and respects the animals it keeps.

lessons.title: Young People Should Buy Fewer, Better-Quality Clothes
lessons.topic: Young People Should Buy Fewer, Better-Quality Clothes
lessons.passage: A wardrobe does not need to be full to be useful. Buying fewer clothes that fit well, last longer and can be worn in different situations may be better than constantly buying new items. This approach can save money over time and reduce clothing waste. Young people should still be able to enjoy fashion and express their style. Second-hand clothes, clothing swaps and careful choices can also be part of that. Quality does not always mean an expensive brand; it means choosing something we will genuinely use. For me, thinking before buying is more important than keeping up with every new trend.

lessons.title: Fast Fashion Encourages Too Much Waste
lessons.topic: Fast Fashion Encourages Too Much Waste
lessons.passage: Fast fashion makes trendy clothes cheap and easy to buy, which can be attractive to teenagers who want to change styles often. The problem is that low prices can encourage people to treat clothing as disposable. Items may be worn only a few times before they are forgotten or thrown away, creating more waste. Not every family can afford expensive brands, and higher price does not always mean better quality. So the solution is not simply “buy expensive clothes”. The better habit is buying less, choosing items we will actually wear and taking care of them for longer.

lessons.title: Single-Use Plastic Should Be Reduced at School Events
lessons.topic: Single-Use Plastic Should Be Reduced at School Events
lessons.passage: School festivals and celebrations can create a surprising amount of waste from cups, bottles, bags and decorations used for only a few hours. Schools should reduce single-use plastic where practical. Reusable water bottles, refill stations and durable decorations can make a difference across many events. Not every disposable item can be removed, especially when hygiene and safety are involved. The goal should be realistic improvement rather than a perfect zero-waste event. School activities are also educational opportunities. When students see waste being reduced in real situations, environmental responsibility becomes something they practise instead of only discussing in class.

lessons.title: Cities Should Create More Safe Spaces for Walking and Cycling
lessons.topic: Cities Should Create More Safe Spaces for Walking and Cycling
lessons.passage: Many people would walk or cycle more often if the route felt safe. Busy traffic, missing pavements and unclear crossings can make short journeys difficult, especially for young people. Cities can improve this by creating better pavements, safe crossings and protected cycle lanes where they are practical. Road space is limited, so changes need careful planning and cannot happen everywhere at once. Cars and motorbikes will still be necessary for many journeys. But giving people safer choices can reduce traffic on some trips and support physical activity. I think streets should be designed for people moving in different ways, not only for vehicles.

lessons.title: Public Transport Should Be Cheaper for Students
lessons.topic: Public Transport Should Be Cheaper for Students
lessons.passage: Students often depend on adults for transport because they do not yet drive, which can make buses and other public services especially important. Lower student fares would make travel to school, libraries and activities more affordable for families. It could also encourage young people to become comfortable using public transport instead of expecting a private vehicle for every journey. Transport systems still need money to operate safely, so completely free travel may not always be realistic. A reasonable student discount is a more balanced option. Public transport should be priced so that young people can actually use the service, not only know that it exists.

lessons.title: Online Privacy Is More Important Than Online Popularity
lessons.topic: Online Privacy Is More Important Than Online Popularity
lessons.passage: Young people may feel pressure to post more photos, personal stories or location details because popular accounts seem very open. But online popularity is temporary, while personal information can be difficult to take back once it has been shared. Privacy settings help, but screenshots and copied posts can still travel beyond the original audience. This does not mean teenagers should never share anything online. They simply need to think about what belongs in public and what should stay private. Protecting personal information is more valuable than gaining extra likes or followers because privacy affects real safety and can matter for years.

lessons.title: Students Should Not Submit AI-Generated Work as Their Own
lessons.topic: Students Should Not Submit AI-Generated Work as Their Own
lessons.passage: If AI writes an assignment and a student submits it as personal work, the teacher can no longer see what the student actually understands. The problem is not simply that technology was used; it is that the authorship is hidden. Students may use AI in ways the teacher allows, such as brainstorming or checking language, but they should be honest about the process. Copying generated text also removes the struggle that often produces real learning. Schools need clear rules because acceptable AI use may differ by task. I think the basic principle is straightforward: assistance can be useful, but work presented as your own should genuinely represent your own thinking.

lessons.title: AI Can Improve Education If Students Use It Responsibly
lessons.topic: AI Can Improve Education If Students Use It Responsibly
lessons.passage: AI can give students quick explanations, extra examples and feedback at times when a teacher is not available. It can also help them practise languages or explore different ways to understand a difficult idea. These benefits depend on responsible use. Students still need to verify information, protect personal data and do the thinking required by the task. Teachers also need to explain when AI is appropriate and when work must be completed independently. I do not think AI will improve education simply by being present. It will improve education only when schools teach students to use it as a thoughtful tool rather than an easy shortcut.

lessons.title: Teenagers Should Not Use Phones During Family Meals
lessons.topic: Teenagers Should Not Use Phones During Family Meals
lessons.passage: A family meal is a small daily opportunity to pay attention to the people sitting in the same room. Using a phone during that time can send the message that whatever is on the screen matters more than the conversation. Teenagers should put phones away, but adults should follow the same rule so that it feels fair. There can be reasonable exceptions, such as an urgent call or an important family message. The aim is not to control every minute of phone use. It is to protect one short period for face-to-face connection. For busy families, that simple habit can make shared meals feel more meaningful.

lessons.title: Parents Should Set Rules for Online Gaming
lessons.topic: Parents Should Set Rules for Online Gaming
lessons.passage: Online games can be social, challenging and enjoyable, but they are designed to keep players interested for a long time. Younger teenagers may therefore need clear family rules about when gaming happens and how long it lasts. Rules can also cover spending money in games and talking to strangers online. Parents should listen to the child’s point of view rather than setting random limits that are impossible to follow. As teenagers show responsibility, they can have more control over their own schedule. I think good gaming rules are not about punishment; they are about making sure games fit into life instead of pushing out sleep, study and family time.

lessons.title: Influencers Should Clearly Label Paid Advertising
lessons.topic: Influencers Should Clearly Label Paid Advertising
lessons.passage: When an influencer recommends a product, young viewers may believe it is simply a personal opinion. If the company has paid for that recommendation, the audience deserves to know. Clear labels such as “advertisement” or “sponsored” help people understand the relationship behind the message. This does not mean the influencer must dislike the product or that all paid content is dishonest. The important issue is transparency. Young people are learning how advertising works, and hidden promotion makes that harder. Anyone with influence over a large audience should clearly separate normal content from advertising that earns them money.

lessons.title: The Minimum Age for Social Media Should Be Enforced More Strictly
lessons.topic: The Minimum Age for Social Media Should Be Enforced More Strictly
lessons.passage: Many platforms have minimum-age rules, but younger children can sometimes create accounts simply by entering a different birthday. If an age limit exists for safety reasons, platforms should take it more seriously. Younger users may be less prepared for privacy problems, harmful contact or pressure from online content. Age checks also need to respect privacy, so the solution cannot require children to share unnecessary personal data. Parents still have an important role because no technical system will be perfect. Stronger enforcement would not solve every online problem, but it would make the stated rule more meaningful than a box that almost anyone can click through.

lessons.title: Social Media Does More Harm Than Good for Younger Teens
lessons.topic: Social Media Does More Harm Than Good for Younger Teens
lessons.passage: Social media can help younger teens communicate and discover interesting content, so it is not completely negative. However, the risks are especially strong at this age. Constant comparison, pressure to be popular and endless scrolling can take time away from sleep, study and face-to-face friendships. Young users may also share personal information before they fully understand privacy. Good family rules and careful use can reduce some of these problems. Still, younger teens do not need every social platform simply because their friends have it. For this age group, the disadvantages often outweigh the benefits unless use is limited and well guided.

lessons.title: Schools Should Teach Debate as a Regular Skill
lessons.topic: Schools Should Teach Debate as a Regular Skill
lessons.passage: Debate should not be limited to special competitions or students who are already confident speakers. Regular classroom debate can teach everyone how to organise an argument, support it with reasons and respond to another point of view. It also gives students a reason to listen carefully because a good rebuttal depends on understanding what the other side actually said. Topics should be suitable for the age group and the classroom should remain respectful. The aim is not to create arguments between students. It is to practise reasoning and communication. I think debate belongs in normal education because these skills are useful in speaking, writing and everyday decision-making.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn How to Work with People They Disagree With
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn How to Work with People They Disagree With
lessons.passage: In group work, students do not always choose their partners, and they will not always share the same ideas. That can be frustrating, but it is also useful practice for real life. Students should learn to listen actively, explain their own point of view and look for a reasonable compromise when possible. Working together does not require everyone to pretend they agree. It requires respect and a focus on the shared task. Teachers can model language for disagreeing without attacking another person. This skill is important because future workplaces and communities will include people with very different opinions and personalities.

lessons.title: Arts Education Should Be Protected in Busy School Schedules
lessons.topic: Arts Education Should Be Protected in Busy School Schedules
lessons.passage: When school schedules become crowded, art and music are sometimes treated as subjects that can be reduced first. That is a mistake. Arts education develops creativity, observation, practice and ways of expressing ideas that are different from written tests. It can also give students a valuable mental break from a day filled with academic tasks. This does not mean art should replace Maths, languages or Science. A balanced curriculum needs different forms of learning. Protecting some regular time for the arts sends the message that education is about developing the whole person, not only the skills that are easiest to examine.

lessons.title: Sports Should Be for Everyone, Not Only Strong Athletes
lessons.topic: Sports Should Be for Everyone, Not Only Strong Athletes
lessons.passage: School sport often celebrates the fastest runners and strongest players, but physical activity should benefit every student. PE can include different kinds of movement so that students with different abilities have ways to participate and improve. Competitive teams are still valuable for students who want a higher level of challenge. The problem comes when less athletic students begin to feel that sport is not for them at all. Schools can teach skills, fitness and teamwork without expecting everyone to perform at the same level. The main goal of school sport should be helping all students build a positive relationship with physical activity.

lessons.title: Schools Should Reduce Competitive Ranking
lessons.passage: Ranking students from highest to lowest may motivate a few people, but it can also make learning feel like a constant competition. Students develop at different speeds and have different strengths, so one list cannot describe their full ability. Schools can still recognise excellent achievement without publicly comparing everyone all the time. Showing individual progress gives students a clearer idea of what they need to improve. Some healthy competition can be enjoyable, especially in voluntary contests. But as a general school culture, I think progress should matter more than position. Students need reasons to learn that do not depend on beating the person beside them.

lessons.title: Students Should Take Part in Community Service
lessons.topic: Students Should Take Part in Community Service
lessons.passage: Community service gives students a chance to use time and skills for something beyond themselves. Activities might include environmental clean-ups, school charity projects or helping younger learners under adult supervision. The experience can develop empathy and social responsibility, especially when students understand who the activity helps and why. Service should be age-appropriate and should not take so much time that it harms schoolwork or family life. I also think reflection matters more than collecting certificates. When students connect an activity with a real community need, volunteering becomes more than a task; it becomes a lesson in participation.

lessons.title: Every School Should Have a Reading Culture, Not Just a Library
lessons.topic: Every School Should Have a Reading Culture, Not Just a Library
lessons.passage: A room full of books does not automatically create readers. A real reading culture appears when books are talked about, recommended and enjoyed across the school. Teachers can share short recommendations, students can exchange favourite titles and libraries can display different genres in inviting ways. Reading should not always be followed by a test or worksheet, because that can make every book feel like an assignment. Not every student will become an enthusiastic reader, and that is okay. Still, schools should make reading visible and social so that students have more chances to discover a book that genuinely interests them.

lessons.title: School Canteens Should Offer Healthier Choices
lessons.topic: School Canteens Should Offer Healthier Choices
lessons.passage: Students are more likely to choose healthy food when it is easy to find, tastes good and is affordable. School canteens can help by offering water, fruit and balanced meals alongside occasional treats. I do not think every sweet or fried item needs to be removed. Strict rules can make food feel more complicated than necessary. The better approach is to make healthier options normal and attractive rather than expecting students to choose them when only less healthy food is convenient. A school cannot control every meal a child eats, but it can create an environment that supports sensible choices during the hours students spend there.

lessons.title: Schools Should Provide More Quiet Spaces for Students
lessons.topic: Schools Should Provide More Quiet Spaces for Students
lessons.passage: Schools are busy places full of voices, movement and activity. Most of that energy is positive, but some students occasionally need a quieter place to read, study or calm down. A library corner, supervised study room or peaceful outdoor area can provide that option. Quiet spaces should not be used to isolate students or remove them from normal school life. They are simply another environment for students who need a short break from noise. A school that offers different kinds of spaces recognises that students do not all learn or recharge in exactly the same way.

lessons.title: School Uniforms Should Be Practical Rather Than Formal
lessons.topic: School Uniforms Should Be Practical Rather Than Formal
lessons.passage: A uniform can create school identity, but students wear it for many hours while sitting, walking and sometimes playing outside. For everyday use, comfort and practicality should matter more than looking extremely formal. In Vietnam’s hot weather, breathable material and a design that allows easy movement can make a real difference. Schools can still keep colours and styles that look neat and represent the school community. Special ceremonies may need more formal clothing. But on normal days, a uniform should be designed around the students who have to learn in it, not only around how it looks in a photograph.

lessons.title: Students Should Have a Voice in School Rules
lessons.topic: Students Should Have a Voice in School Rules
lessons.passage: Adults are responsible for safety and learning, so students cannot make every school rule themselves. However, rules often work better when students understand the reason behind them and have a chance to share their views. A student council or class discussion could give feedback on issues such as break areas, phone rules or school activities. Listening does not mean adults must agree with every request. Some boundaries are necessary even when they are unpopular. Student voice matters because young people are more likely to respect a system when they feel they are part of the conversation rather than only receiving orders.

lessons.title: Schools Should Offer More Clubs Instead of More Extra Classes
lessons.topic: Schools Should Offer More Clubs Instead of More Extra Classes
lessons.passage: Extra academic classes can be useful when students need support, but a school week should not be filled only with more studying. Clubs give young people space to explore interests such as art, sport, science, music, debate or photography. They can develop skills and friendships that are difficult to build in a normal lesson. Students who genuinely need extra help should still be able to receive it. The issue is balance, not choosing clubs for everyone. I think schools should protect time for interest-based activities because education should help students discover what they enjoy as well as what they need to pass.

lessons.title: Students Should Have More Practical Life-Skills Lessons
lessons.topic: Students Should Have More Practical Life-Skills Lessons
lessons.passage: School prepares students for exams, but adulthood also includes many small practical tasks that do not appear in textbooks. Life-skills lessons could include basic cooking, first aid, simple sewing, organising personal documents or filling in common forms. These topics should not replace core academic subjects, and some skills are also learned at home. However, not every student has the same opportunities outside school. A small amount of practical teaching can give everyone a useful foundation. Education works best when students leave school able not only to answer questions, but also to handle ordinary responsibilities with confidence.

lessons.title: Schools Should Teach Personal Finance
lessons.passage: Most students will eventually have a bank account, pay bills and make decisions about saving or borrowing money. Yet many people reach adulthood without understanding basic personal finance. Schools could teach simple ideas such as budgeting, comparing prices, saving regularly and understanding how interest works. The lessons should use realistic examples rather than complicated financial products. Families will still make their own decisions about money, and schools should respect different circumstances. Financial education is valuable because it gives every student some basic knowledge before mistakes become much more expensive.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn How Algorithms Shape What They See Online
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn How Algorithms Shape What They See Online
lessons.passage: When two people open the same app, they may see completely different videos and posts. Algorithms use our past behaviour to decide what to recommend next, which can make a feed feel very personal. This is convenient, but it also means we may see more of what keeps our attention rather than a balanced picture of the world. Students do not need to learn computer programming to understand this idea. They simply need to know that the feed is selected, not neutral. This knowledge helps young people make more conscious choices about what they watch, believe and spend time on.

lessons.title: Online Learning Works Best as Part of a Mixed Approach
lessons.topic: Online Learning Works Best as Part of a Mixed Approach
lessons.passage: Online learning can be convenient because students can access materials from home and replay explanations when needed. Face-to-face lessons, however, make it easier to ask questions, work with classmates and receive immediate help. That is why I prefer a mixed approach rather than choosing one system for everything. Digital lessons can support homework, revision or special situations, while classroom time can focus on interaction and guidance. This approach still depends on a reliable internet connection and good planning. I think technology is most useful when it adds flexibility to education without removing the human contact that helps many students learn.

lessons.title: Schools Should Teach Digital Citizenship
lessons.passage: Knowing how to use an app is not the same as knowing how to behave well online. Digital citizenship includes protecting privacy, communicating respectfully and understanding that online actions can leave a lasting digital footprint. Students should also know when to report harmful behaviour and why sharing another person’s photo without permission can be a problem. Families have an important role, but schools can give all students a shared set of principles. These lessons should be practical rather than frightening. Young people need to learn that the same values we expect face to face—respect, responsibility and honesty—also matter behind a screen.

lessons.title: Phones Should Stay Away During Most Lessons
lessons.topic: Phones Should Stay Away During Most Lessons
lessons.passage: A smartphone can be a dictionary, camera or research tool, but it is also a powerful source of distraction. Even one notification can pull attention away from a lesson and make it difficult to focus again. For most lessons, phones should stay in bags or another agreed place unless the teacher gives permission to use them. This is not the same as banning phones from school completely. There may be useful learning activities or practical reasons for having a device available. The rule simply makes the default clear: during learning time, attention belongs to the lesson, not to whatever appears on the screen.

lessons.title: AI Should Be Used as a Learning Assistant, Not an Answer Machine
lessons.topic: AI Should Be Used as a Learning Assistant, Not an Answer Machine
lessons.passage: AI can explain a difficult idea, suggest practice questions or give feedback on a draft, which makes it a useful learning assistant. The problem begins when students ask it to complete a task and then submit the answer without thinking. That may produce finished work but not real learning. Students also need to verify AI responses because they can be incomplete or wrong. Teachers should show students how to write useful prompts and when AI is allowed. For me, the best rule is simple: use AI to help your thinking, not replace it. The final work should still show what the student understands and can do.

lessons.title: Students Should Be Allowed to Correct Major Assignments
lessons.topic: Students Should Be Allowed to Correct Major Assignments
lessons.passage: A teacher’s feedback is most useful when students have a chance to do something with it. For major assignments, students should sometimes be allowed to revise their work and submit a second draft. This forces them to look again at weak ideas, unclear language or mistakes instead of only checking the final mark. The first attempt should still matter, so correction should not become an easy way to avoid preparing properly. Teachers can set clear limits on what may be changed. The purpose is not to give everyone a perfect grade. It is to make revision part of learning rather than something students only hear about.

lessons.title: Exams Should Not Be the Only Measure of Learning
lessons.topic: Exams Should Not Be the Only Measure of Learning
lessons.passage: Exams can show what students remember and how well they work under a time limit, so they have a useful place in education. But they cannot measure every kind of learning. A student may be strong at research, teamwork, speaking or creative problem-solving even if written exams are difficult for them. Projects, classroom work and presentations can provide other evidence of progress. Using several forms of assessment does not mean making standards lower. It means collecting a fuller picture. Important decisions about a student should not depend on one type of test when learning itself is much broader.

lessons.title: Schools Should Have Regular Speaking and Presentation Practice
lessons.topic: Schools Should Have Regular Speaking and Presentation Practice
lessons.passage: Students are often asked to speak in front of others only when an important presentation is graded. That can make public speaking feel much more frightening than it needs to be. Short, regular practice can build confidence gradually. Students might explain an answer, introduce a book, present a mind map or give a one-minute opinion. They can learn to use a clear voice, organise ideas and make natural eye contact. Not every task needs to be performed in front of the whole class; pairs and small groups are useful steps too. I think speaking should be treated as a skill we practise, not a test we suddenly face.

lessons.title: Students Should Be Taught How to Give Useful Feedback
lessons.topic: Students Should Be Taught How to Give Useful Feedback
lessons.passage: Saying “It is good” or “It is bad” does not help a classmate improve very much. Students should learn how to give feedback that is specific, constructive and kind. For example, they can mention one thing that works well and one clear suggestion for the next version. They also need to comment on the work rather than attack the person. Peer feedback should not replace the teacher, and students need guidance before using it. Still, it is a valuable skill because giving thoughtful feedback makes us examine ideas more carefully. It also teaches us how to disagree or suggest change without being rude.

lessons.title: Schools Should Teach Note-Taking Skills
lessons.passage: Many students copy everything a teacher writes because they have never been shown another way to take notes. Schools should teach how to identify key ideas, use keywords and summarise information in a shorter form. Different methods can work, including lists, tables, diagrams and mind maps. Students should be encouraged to find a system that helps them remember rather than produce the neatest page. Good notes are especially useful when revising because they make important information easier to find. Note-taking is a basic study skill, and teaching it directly can save students a lot of time later.

lessons.title: Group Work Should Include Individual Responsibility
lessons.topic: Group Work Should Include Individual Responsibility
lessons.passage: Group work can be excellent for discussion and teamwork, but it becomes frustrating when one student does most of the task. Each member should have a clear responsibility, such as researching, writing, designing or presenting. The group still needs to share ideas and help one another, but individual roles make contributions easier to see. Teachers should also avoid making roles too rigid because students need to practise different skills over time. Successful group work combines cooperation with personal responsibility. Students learn to depend on one another without learning that someone else will always finish the work for them.

lessons.title: Students Should Be Allowed to Choose Some Project Topics
lessons.topic: Students Should Be Allowed to Choose Some Project Topics
lessons.passage: Students often put more effort into a project when they are genuinely interested in the subject. Teachers could give a broad theme and allow students to choose a smaller topic within it. For example, a project on the environment might include plastic waste, local wildlife or saving electricity. Choice creates a sense of ownership and can make research more meaningful. However, complete freedom may lead to topics that are too easy, too difficult or unrelated to the lesson. Clear guidelines are still needed. I think the best approach combines teacher direction with enough student choice to keep curiosity alive.

lessons.title: Homework Should Focus on Quality, Not Quantity
lessons.topic: Homework Should Focus on Quality, Not Quantity
lessons.passage: A long homework sheet is not automatically better than a short one. The important question is whether the task has a clear purpose. A few well-chosen exercises can help students practise a difficult skill, while large amounts of repetitive work may simply make them tired. Homework should also leave enough time for sleep, family and activities outside school. Some subjects sometimes need more practice, especially before an important assessment. But as a regular approach, teachers should choose work for its learning value rather than its length. Quality homework helps students understand more; quantity alone only makes the bag heavier.

lessons.title: A Good Friend Does Not Have to Agree with You
lessons.topic: A Good Friend Does Not Have to Agree with You
lessons.passage: Friendship would be very difficult if people had to agree about everything. Good friends can like different music, support different ideas or make different choices and still respect one another. In fact, an honest friend may sometimes tell us something we do not want to hear. What matters is how the disagreement is handled. Insults, pressure and refusing to listen can damage a friendship, while calm discussion can make it stronger. A good friend is not someone who always says “yes”. It is someone who can disagree with us and still care about our feelings and our point of view.

lessons.title: Young People Should Learn to Spot Advertising Tricks
lessons.topic: Young People Should Learn to Spot Advertising Tricks
lessons.passage: Advertising is designed to persuade us, and young people see it everywhere from videos to games and social media. Understanding common tricks can help them make better choices. An advert may use a celebrity, a limited-time offer or exciting music to make a product feel more necessary than it really is. This does not mean every advertisement is dishonest. Companies have a right to explain what they sell. But students should learn to ask who the target audience is and what the advert wants them to feel. That small pause can turn an automatic reaction into a thoughtful decision.

lessons.title: Public Libraries Are Still Important
lessons.passage: People can find enormous amounts of information online, but that does not make public libraries unnecessary. Libraries give people free or low-cost access to books, study spaces and useful resources. For students who do not have a quiet room or many books at home, that access can matter a lot. Modern libraries can also offer clubs, workshops and digital materials rather than only shelves of printed books. Of course, libraries need to change with the way people learn. I think their purpose is still valuable: giving everyone in the community a welcoming place to read, study and discover information.

lessons.title: Every Teenager Should Know Basic First Aid
lessons.topic: Every Teenager Should Know Basic First Aid
lessons.passage: Teenagers spend time at school, sports activities and places where an adult may not be standing beside them every second. Basic first aid can help them respond calmly to a small injury and recognise when professional help is needed. They can learn how to deal with minor cuts, use a bandage, call emergency services correctly and avoid moving someone when it may be unsafe. A short course cannot turn students into doctors, and they should never take unnecessary risks. Still, knowing what to do in the first few minutes of a problem can be extremely useful. For that reason, basic first aid belongs in every teenager’s life skills.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn to Cook One Complete Meal
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn to Cook One Complete Meal
lessons.passage: Making a snack is useful, but preparing one complete meal teaches a wider set of skills. Students need to choose a simple recipe, collect ingredients, organise the order of steps and follow kitchen safety rules. The meal could be something familiar such as rice with a simple dish and vegetables, noodles, soup or another family recipe. Young people should work with adult guidance until they can use equipment safely. The goal is not a perfect restaurant meal. It is learning to prepare real food from beginning to end. Being able to cook one complete meal is a useful step towards independence.

lessons.title: Healthy Eating Should Be About Balance, Not Strict Rules
lessons.topic: Healthy Eating Should Be About Balance, Not Strict Rules
lessons.passage: Healthy eating is important, but it can become confusing when food is divided into things we are “allowed” or “not allowed” to eat. A better approach is to think about balance and variety over time. Most meals can include nutritious foods such as vegetables, fruit, rice, protein and water, while sweets or fried foods can still be enjoyed sometimes. Different families also eat in different ways, so one perfect menu does not exist. Young people should learn how food supports health without becoming afraid of normal treats. For me, healthy eating means making sensible choices most of the time, not following strict rules every minute.

lessons.title: It Is Better to Spend Money on Experiences Than Fashion
lessons.topic: It Is Better to Spend Money on Experiences Than Fashion
lessons.passage: Clothes are necessary, and enjoying fashion is not a problem. However, buying new items simply to follow every trend can use a lot of money without creating much lasting value. The same money might pay for a short trip, a class, a concert or another experience shared with people we care about. Experiences often leave memories and sometimes teach us something new. That does not mean we should never buy nice clothes. We all have different interests and needs. But if I had extra money to choose between another fashionable item and a meaningful experience, I would usually choose the experience.

However, buying new items simply to follow every trend can use a lot of money without creating much lasting value.
The same money might pay for a short trip, a class, a concert or another experience shared with people we care about.
Experiences often leave memories and sometimes teach us something new.
That does not mean we should never buy nice clothes.
We all have different interests and needs.
But if I had extra money to choose between another fashionable item and a meaningful experience, I would usually choose the experience.

lessons.title: Parents Should Give Teenagers More Responsibility as They Grow
lessons.topic: Parents Should Give Teenagers More Responsibility as They Grow
lessons.passage: Teenagers cannot learn responsibility if adults make every decision for them. As they grow, they should gradually take charge of more tasks, such as managing homework, helping at home, planning small journeys or looking after their own belongings. More responsibility should come with clear boundaries and should match the teenager’s age and maturity. Parents still need to step in when safety is involved. Trust should also be earned through reliable behaviour. This gradual approach works better than either controlling everything or suddenly expecting a young person to manage adult responsibilities without practice.

lessons.title: Teenagers Should Learn How to Plan Their Time
lessons.topic: Teenagers Should Learn How to Plan Their Time
lessons.passage: As students get older, schoolwork, hobbies and family responsibilities all compete for the same hours. Time management helps them decide what needs to be done first instead of reacting to every task at the last minute. A simple schedule can include deadlines, study periods and free time. Plans should not be so strict that one unexpected event ruins the whole day. The real goal is to reduce procrastination and create balance. Learning to organise time in secondary school is especially useful because later there will be fewer adults reminding students about every deadline.

lessons.title: Learning from Failure Is More Important Than Always Getting High Marks
lessons.topic: Learning from Failure Is More Important Than Always Getting High Marks
lessons.passage: High marks can be satisfying, but they do not teach us everything about learning. Sometimes the most useful lesson comes from getting something wrong, understanding why and trying again. Failure can develop resilience because it shows us that one poor result does not have to be the end of the story. This does not mean marks are unimportant or that students should stop trying to do well. Good results can show real effort and knowledge. But if students become afraid of every mistake, they may avoid difficult challenges. Learning how to recover from failure is a skill that lasts longer than any single test score.

lessons.title: Keeping a Journal Can Help Teenagers Understand Themselves
lessons.topic: Keeping a Journal Can Help Teenagers Understand Themselves
lessons.passage: Teenage years can bring many changes in school, friendships and feelings. Writing in a journal gives young people a private place to organise their thoughts without needing an immediate answer from anyone else. They can record a good day, explain why something upset them or think about a decision they need to make. A journal is not useful for everyone, and it should never become compulsory personal writing for other people to read. But for students who enjoy writing, it can be a helpful way to reflect. Looking back later may also show how much they have changed and grown.

lessons.title: Young People Should Volunteer in Their Community
lessons.topic: Young People Should Volunteer in Their Community
lessons.passage: Young people may not have much money to give, but they can still contribute time and effort. They might help at a local clean-up, support a school charity event, read with younger children or assist elderly people in simple ways. Volunteering can teach responsibility and show students that communities improve when people help one another. The activity should be safe, age-appropriate and genuinely useful rather than done only for a certificate. Students also need enough time for school and rest. Occasional volunteering is valuable because it turns kindness from an idea into something we actually do.

lessons.title: Travelling with Family Is a Good Way to Learn
lessons.topic: Travelling with Family Is a Good Way to Learn
lessons.passage: Travel can teach things that are difficult to understand from a textbook alone. A family trip may introduce young people to a different landscape, local food, history or way of life. Even a short trip within Vietnam can involve planning routes, reading signs and learning about another place. Travel does not need to be expensive or international to be educational. Families also need time to rest, so every holiday should not become a school lesson. Still, exploring places together creates useful experiences and memories. When we see something for ourselves, the learning often stays with us longer.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn How to Manage Stress
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn How to Manage Stress
lessons.passage: School cannot remove every stressful situation, but it can help students respond to stress in healthier ways. Young people can learn simple habits such as breaking large tasks into smaller steps, taking short breaks, sleeping enough and talking to someone when a problem feels too big. Different strategies work for different people, so stress management should not become another rule students are judged on. Serious or continuing problems also need support from trusted adults or professionals. Learning these skills early is useful because pressure does not disappear after school. Knowing when to pause and ask for help is a strength, not a weakness.

lessons.title: A Hobby Does Not Need to Become a Competition
lessons.topic: A Hobby Does Not Need to Become a Competition
lessons.passage: Competition can motivate people, but not every hobby needs a winner, a medal or a ranking. Sometimes we draw, play music, run or bake simply because the activity makes us happy. Turning every interest into a competition can create pressure and make people compare themselves too much. Of course, students who enjoy contests should have the chance to enter them and challenge themselves. Others may prefer to improve at their own speed. I think hobbies are valuable because they give us enjoyment and balance. Success can mean getting better, learning something new or simply wanting to continue.

lessons.title: Real Friendships Matter More Than Having Many Online Followers
lessons.topic: Real Friendships Matter More Than Having Many Online Followers
lessons.passage: A large number of followers can make someone look popular online, but numbers do not tell us who will actually support us when life is difficult. Real friendships grow through shared experiences, trust and time together. A good friend notices when we are upset, listens to us and can disagree without disappearing. Online friendships can also be meaningful, especially when people share interests and behave safely. The problem comes when popularity becomes more important than connection. I would rather have a small group of people I truly trust than thousands of followers who know almost nothing about me.

lessons.title: Teenagers Should Get Enough Sleep Even If It Means Less Screen Time
lessons.topic: Teenagers Should Get Enough Sleep Even If It Means Less Screen Time
lessons.passage: It is easy to lose track of time when watching videos, gaming or messaging friends at night. Unfortunately, the next school morning still arrives at the same time. Teenagers need enough sleep to concentrate, remember information and manage their mood. If screen time regularly pushes bedtime later, then the screen should be the thing that changes. There will always be special nights when routines are different. But as a normal habit, sleep should come first. A phone can wait until tomorrow; a tired brain has to get through the whole school day.

lessons.title: Everyone Should Have Some Time Alone
lessons.topic: Everyone Should Have Some Time Alone
lessons.passage: Being social is important, but being alone for a while is not the same as being lonely. After a busy school day, some people need quiet time to read, listen to music, draw or simply think. Personal space can help us recharge and understand our own feelings without constant noise or messages. Other people may prefer more company, so there is no single amount of alone time that suits everyone. The important thing is having a healthy choice. Young people should learn that it is normal to enjoy both friendship and quiet time, rather than feeling they must always be available.

lessons.title: Young People Should Learn Basic Repair Skills
lessons.topic: Young People Should Learn Basic Repair Skills
lessons.passage: When something small breaks, our first thought is often to throw it away and buy another one. Basic repair skills can change that habit. Young people can learn simple tasks such as sewing on a button, tightening a loose screw or fixing a bicycle tyre with adult guidance. These skills save money and help us understand how everyday objects work. Safety matters, so students should not attempt electrical or dangerous repairs themselves. Still, learning to fix simple things is practical and environmentally friendly. It teaches us that not everything needs to be replaced the moment it stops working perfectly.

lessons.title: It Is Better to Save for One Good Item Than Buy Many Cheap Things
lessons.topic: It Is Better to Save for One Good Item Than Buy Many Cheap Things
lessons.passage: Cheap items can seem like a good deal because we can buy more of them with the same amount of money. The problem is that some low-quality products break quickly and need to be replaced. Saving for one durable school bag, pair of shoes or piece of equipment may cost more at first but last much longer. Price alone does not guarantee quality, so we still need to compare products carefully. Sometimes a cheaper item is completely suitable. But when something will be used often, choosing quality over quantity can save money and reduce waste in the long run.

lessons.title: Spending Time Outdoors Is Important for Teenagers
lessons.topic: Spending Time Outdoors Is Important for Teenagers
lessons.passage: Teenagers often spend long hours indoors at school, doing homework or using screens. Regular outdoor time gives the body a chance to move and the mind a break from the same environment. It does not have to mean organised sport; walking, cycling, helping in a garden or meeting friends in a park all count. Weather and traffic can make outdoor activities difficult in some places, so the idea needs to be practical. Still, outdoor time should be part of a normal week. It supports physical health, reduces screen time and can make everyday routines feel less tiring.

lessons.title: Learning to Cook Is as Important as Learning to Use Technology
lessons.topic: Learning to Cook Is as Important as Learning to Use Technology
lessons.passage: Young people are often very confident with phones and apps, but some are less confident in the kitchen. Both kinds of skill matter. Technology helps us study, communicate and work, while cooking helps us care for ourselves every day. Knowing how to prepare a few simple meals can save money and make healthy choices easier later in life. No one needs to become an expert cook at this age. Starting with safe, basic recipes is enough. A good education should prepare students for real life, and being able to feed ourselves is one of the most practical skills there is.

lessons.title: Teenagers Should Help Plan Family Meals
lessons.topic: Teenagers Should Help Plan Family Meals
lessons.passage: Planning meals may look like an adult job, but teenagers can learn a lot by taking part. They can suggest dishes, check what ingredients are already at home and think about whether the meal is balanced. This helps them understand nutrition, food costs and the work that happens before food reaches the table. Teenagers should not be expected to organise every meal, especially in busy families. Even helping with one dinner a week is enough to practise. I think being involved in meal planning is a practical way to become more responsible and appreciate the effort behind everyday family life.

lessons.title: Reading for Pleasure Should Be Part of Every Week
lessons.topic: Reading for Pleasure Should Be Part of Every Week
lessons.passage: Students read a lot for school, but reading because we want to is different. A novel, comic, biography or science book can give us new ideas without feeling like another assignment. Regular reading also builds vocabulary and concentration naturally because we meet words in meaningful situations. Not every student enjoys the same genre, so forcing everyone to read the same kind of book may have the opposite effect. Schools and families can help by making different books easy to find. Even a small amount of enjoyable reading each week can build a habit that lasts far beyond school.

lessons.title: Keeping a Personal Study Plan Is Better Than Studying Only Before Tests
lessons.topic: Keeping a Personal Study Plan Is Better Than Studying Only Before Tests
lessons.passage: Studying only when a test is close can turn learning into a stressful race. A simple study plan spreads the work across the week and makes progress easier to see. Students can decide when to review vocabulary, finish assignments or practise a difficult subject instead of leaving everything until the last minute. The plan should stay flexible because school weeks are not always predictable. It should not fill every hour with study either. For me, a realistic plan is useful because it creates regular habits while still leaving room for rest, hobbies and family life.

lessons.title: Young People Should Learn to Travel Independently in Their Local Area
lessons.topic: Young People Should Learn to Travel Independently in Their Local Area
lessons.passage: As children grow into teenagers, they should gradually learn how to move around their local area safely. This might mean walking to a nearby class, reading a bus route or knowing how to get home from a familiar place. These small experiences build independence and help young people understand directions, traffic and public transport. Of course, independence should grow step by step and depend on the area, distance and maturity of the student. Parents still need to set clear safety rules. The aim is not to send young people everywhere alone, but to prepare them to manage everyday journeys responsibly.

lessons.title: Students Need at Least One Screen-Free Hobby
lessons.topic: Students Need at Least One Screen-Free Hobby
lessons.passage: Screens are useful for study, entertainment and communication, but they can easily fill every free minute. That is why I think students need at least one hobby that does not depend on a phone, tablet or computer. It might be badminton, drawing, gardening, reading, baking or playing an instrument. A screen-free hobby gives the eyes and mind a different kind of break and may help students discover a real interest. Digital hobbies can be creative too, so there is no need to reject them. The goal is balance: young people should have more than one way to relax and enjoy themselves.

lessons.title: Family Meals Should Be Phone-Free
lessons.passage: Family members are often busy at different times of the day, so a shared meal can be one of the few moments when everyone is together. If each person is checking a phone, that moment easily disappears. Keeping phones away allows people to ask about school, work or plans and actually listen to the answers. There may be exceptions, such as an urgent call, and the rule should apply to adults as well as children. This is not about saying phones are bad. It is about protecting a short part of the day for real conversation, which makes family relationships stronger.

lessons.title: Teenagers Should Have a Weekly Budget
lessons.topic: Teenagers Should Have a Weekly Budget
lessons.passage: As teenagers become more independent, they start making more small money decisions for themselves. A weekly budget can help them see how quickly snacks, drinks or small purchases add up. Instead of spending first and thinking later, they can decide how much to save and what expenses are really worth it. The amount does not need to be large; the lesson comes from planning. Parents can still give advice, especially at the beginning. Learning to manage a small budget now is much safer than waiting until adulthood to learn through expensive mistakes.

lessons.title: It Is Better to Learn a Skill Than Buy a New Gadget
lessons.topic: It Is Better to Learn a Skill Than Buy a New Gadget
lessons.passage: A new gadget can be exciting, especially when many friends are talking about it. However, I would rather spend time or money learning a useful skill, such as swimming, cooking, photography or playing an instrument. A device may feel old after a few years, while a skill can stay with us and improve as we practise. Skills can also give us confidence and open new opportunities. Of course, technology can be useful and sometimes we genuinely need a new device. But when the choice is only about enjoyment, investing in something we can learn and keep is usually more valuable.

lessons.title: Every Primary Student Should Learn How to Debate
lessons.topic: Every Primary Student Should Learn How to Debate
lessons.passage:
I think debate is a useful skill for primary students when it is taught in a simple and friendly way.
Children can learn to say what they think, give reasons and listen carefully to someone who has a different opinion.
They also learn that disagreeing does not mean being rude.
A good debate is not about shouting louder than the other person.
It is about explaining ideas clearly and responding respectfully.
Debate can improve speaking confidence, thinking skills and even writing.
We do not need difficult topics at primary school.
Starting with familiar questions about school, family and everyday life is enough to build strong habits for the future.

lessons.title: Schools Should Celebrate Kindness as Well as Good Grades
lessons.topic: Schools Should Celebrate Kindness as Well as Good Grades
lessons.passage:
Good grades are worth celebrating because they can show hard work and progress.
But school is also a place where children learn how to treat other people.
A student who welcomes a new classmate, helps someone who is struggling or behaves respectfully is doing something valuable too.
Schools do not need to give prizes for every kind action.
Sometimes simple recognition is enough.
I think children should understand that being successful is not only about test scores.
Knowledge matters, but kindness helps make the whole school community better.

lessons.title: Students Should Be Allowed to Correct Their Mistakes
lessons.topic: Students Should Be Allowed to Correct Their Mistakes
lessons.passage:
A wrong answer can show us what we still need to learn.
That is why students should sometimes have a chance to correct their mistakes after receiving feedback.
If we simply see a red mark and move on, we may make the same mistake again.
Correcting it makes us think about what went wrong and how to do better next time.
This does not mean every test must be taken again until everyone gets full marks.
The purpose is learning, not changing every grade.
I think a second look at our mistakes can be more valuable than pretending they never happened.

lessons.title: Sports Day Should Focus More on Participation Than Winning
lessons.topic: Sports Day Should Focus More on Participation Than Winning
lessons.passage:
Winning races and matches can make Sports Day exciting.
But I think the main purpose should be getting students involved and helping them enjoy being active.
Not every child is a strong athlete.
If the day only celebrates winners, some students may feel that sport is not for them.
Schools can still give medals and prizes, but they can also recognise teamwork, effort and participation.
Sports Day should encourage children to move, try something new and support their classmates.
For me, a successful event is one where many students finish the day smiling, not only the fastest ones.

lessons.title: Schools Should Grow Some of Their Own Vegetables
lessons.topic: Schools Should Grow Some of Their Own Vegetables
lessons.passage:
A small vegetable garden could teach students many things at once.
They can learn how seeds grow, how plants need water and sunlight, and where food comes from.
Students can also work together to care for the garden.
Harvesting something they planted themselves can be exciting.
Of course, a school garden needs space and someone to look after it during holidays.
Not every school can grow a lot of food.
But even a few pots of herbs or vegetables can provide a useful hands-on learning experience.

lessons.title: Schools Should Reduce Single-Use Plastic
lessons.passage:
Schools can create a lot of plastic waste through bottles, cups, straws and food packaging.
I think they should try to reduce it where practical.
Students can bring reusable water bottles and lunch boxes, while school events can avoid unnecessary plastic items.
However, replacing everything at once may be difficult or expensive.
Some plastic products are also useful for hygiene or safety.
So the goal should be steady improvement, not a perfect “zero plastic” school overnight.
Even small changes can teach students to think more carefully about what they use and throw away.

lessons.title: Public Transport Should Be Cheaper for Students
lessons.topic: Public Transport Should Be Cheaper for Students
lessons.passage:
Students sometimes need buses or other public transport to travel to school or activities.
I think lower fares for students can help families and encourage young people to use public transport more often.
If more people use buses, there may also be fewer private vehicles on busy roads.
Of course, transport systems still need money to operate safely.
That is why I would support a student discount rather than making every trip completely free.
Public transport should be affordable enough that students can use it when they need it.

lessons.title: Children Should Help Make Some Family Rules
lessons.topic: Children Should Help Make Some Family Rules
lessons.passage:
Parents need to set important family rules because they are responsible for children's safety.
Still, I think children can join some family discussions.
For example, a family could talk together about screen time, bedtime or how to share chores.
Children may understand a rule better when they know why it exists.
They may also follow it more willingly if they have had a chance to share their opinion.
This does not mean children make the final decision about everything.
Parents still need to set clear boundaries.
But listening to one another can make family rules feel fairer and easier to follow.

lessons.title: Parents Should Know How Their Young Children Use Phones
lessons.topic: Parents Should Know How Their Young Children Use Phones
lessons.passage:
Young children are still learning how to use phones safely.
That is why I think parents should know which apps they use, who they communicate with and how much time they spend online.
This is not the same as reading every message forever.
As children become older and more responsible, they should have more privacy.
But younger children still need guidance.
Parents can explain online risks and help when something goes wrong.
Trust is important, but trust grows together with responsibility.
For me, supervision should slowly become lighter as children show that they can make good choices.

lessons.title: Everyone in a Family Should Help with Housework
lessons.topic: Everyone in a Family Should Help with Housework
lessons.passage:
A family home belongs to everyone, so I think housework should be shared.
That does not mean every person needs to do exactly the same job.
Adults may handle difficult tasks, while children can do jobs that suit their age.
A younger child can put toys away, and an older child can help with dishes or laundry.
When everyone contributes, one person does not have to carry all the work.
Housework may not be exciting, but it teaches responsibility.
A family is a team, and teams work better when everyone helps.

lessons.title: Children Should Choose Some of Their After-School Activities
lessons.topic: Children Should Choose Some of Their After-School Activities
lessons.passage:
Parents often choose activities because they want their children to learn useful skills.
That can be helpful, especially when children are young.
But I think older primary students should have some say too.
A child who loves football may not enjoy spending every afternoon at an activity they did not choose.
When children are interested, they often practise more willingly.
Parents can still guide the final decision and think about time, cost and schoolwork.
The best plan is not “children decide everything” or “parents decide everything”.
It is making the choice together.

lessons.title: School Uniforms Can Help Students Feel Part of a School
lessons.topic: School Uniforms Can Help Students Feel Part of a School
lessons.passage:
School uniforms do more than make students look neat.
They can also create a feeling that everyone belongs to the same school community.
This is easy to notice on school trips, sports days or special events when students represent their school together.
Uniforms may also reduce some pressure about what clothes to wear.
However, they should be comfortable and suitable for the weather.
I do not think school identity depends only on clothing.
Good friendships, teachers and school activities matter more.
Still, a practical uniform can be one simple way to help students feel part of a group.

lessons.title: Some Lessons Can Be Taught Online
lessons.topic: Some Lessons Can Be Taught Online
lessons.passage:
Online lessons can be useful in some situations.
Students can learn from home when travelling is difficult, and teachers can share videos or digital materials easily.
However, I would not replace normal classrooms completely.
Young students often learn better when they can talk to the teacher face to face, work with friends and ask for help immediately.
Internet problems can also make online learning frustrating.
I think online lessons are best as another option, not the only option.
Technology gives schools more flexibility, but children still need real classrooms and real people around them.

lessons.title: Watching English Cartoons Can Help Children Learn
lessons.topic: Watching English Cartoons Can Help Children Learn
lessons.passage:
English cartoons can be more than entertainment.
Children hear natural pronunciation, common expressions and short conversations.
Pictures and actions also help us understand words we have not learned before.
A good way to learn is to watch a short scene, listen carefully and repeat one or two useful sentences.
However, simply watching cartoons for hours will not automatically make someone good at English.
Students still need lessons and practice.
For me, cartoons are a helpful extra tool because they make English feel alive and enjoyable.

lessons.topic: Every Child Should Learn a Second Language
lessons.passage:
Learning another language can be difficult, but it can open many doors.
For Vietnamese students, English is especially useful because it is used in many parts of the world.
Young learners do not need to speak perfectly.
They can begin with simple words, songs and conversations.
The most important thing is regular practice.
I think every child should have the chance to learn at least one language besides their mother tongue.

lessons.title: Schools Should Not Give Prizes Only to the Best Students
lessons.topic: Schools Should Not Give Prizes Only to the Best Students
lessons.passage:
Students who achieve excellent results deserve to be recognised.
But I do not think school prizes should only go to the students with the highest marks.
A child who improves greatly, helps classmates or works very hard may also deserve recognition.
Different students have different strengths.
If prizes always go to the same small group, others may stop believing that their effort matters.
Schools do not need to give everyone a prize for everything.
However, they can celebrate different kinds of success.
That sends a better message: doing well is important, but growth, effort and good character matter too.

lessons.title: School Competitions Can Motivate Students
lessons.passage:
Competitions can make school activities exciting.
A spelling contest, sports event or speaking competition may encourage students to practise harder and challenge themselves.
Winning can feel great, but I do not think winning should be the only purpose.
Some children become nervous when there is too much pressure.
Competitions should be fair, friendly and suitable for the students' age.
Schools can also celebrate effort and improvement, not only first place.
Used in the right way, competition can motivate students without making them feel that losing means failure.

lessons.title: Students Should Have Homework-Free Weekends Sometimes
lessons.topic: Students Should Have Homework-Free Weekends Sometimes
lessons.passage:
Homework can help students review, but children also need real breaks from schoolwork.
I think schools could sometimes give students a homework-free weekend.
That would give families time to go out, visit relatives, play sports or simply rest without worrying about unfinished exercises.
I would not make every weekend homework-free.
Students sometimes need to practise or prepare for the following week.
But an occasional break can help children recharge.
Learning is important, but rest is part of learning too.

lessons.title: Pets Should Not Be Given as Surprise Gifts
lessons.topic: Pets Should Not Be Given as Surprise Gifts
lessons.passage:
A puppy or kitten may look like a wonderful surprise gift, but a pet is not a toy.
Animals need food, time, space and care for many years.
The person receiving the pet may not be ready for that responsibility.
Their home may also be unsuitable, or someone in the family may have allergies.
I think getting a pet should be a family decision.
People can still surprise someone with a pet-related gift, such as a toy or book.
But the animal itself should only come home after everyone has agreed and prepared for it.

lessons.title: Zoos Can Be Educational If Animals Are Well Cared For
lessons.topic: Zoos Can Be Educational If Animals Are Well Cared For
lessons.passage:
A zoo can help children learn about animals from different parts of the world.
Seeing a real elephant or giraffe can make a lesson more memorable than only seeing a picture.
Zoos can also teach visitors about wildlife protection.
However, education is not a good excuse for keeping animals in poor conditions.
Animals need enough space, proper food and professional care.
I support zoos only when animal welfare is taken seriously.
A good zoo should help people respect wildlife, not simply give visitors something interesting to look at.

lessons.title: Sugary Drinks Should Not Be Sold at School
lessons.topic: Sugary Drinks Should Not Be Sold at School
lessons.passage:
I do not think sugary drinks need to be part of the normal school day.
If they are sold in the canteen every day, students may choose them instead of water.
School is a place where children spend many hours, so it can help build healthy habits.
Water should be easy to find, and other healthier drinks can be available too.
This does not mean students can never enjoy a soft drink.
A birthday or family outing is different from an everyday school lunch.
For school, I think healthier choices should come first.

lessons.title: Fast Food Should Not Be Sold Close to Schools
lessons.topic: Fast Food Should Not Be Sold Close to Schools
lessons.passage:
When fast food is very easy to buy near school, students may choose it more often than they normally would.
A fried snack or sweet drink sometimes is not a big problem.
The concern is when it becomes an everyday habit.
Schools should encourage healthier food choices, and the area around a school can support that goal.
However, I do not think every food shop near a school needs to be banned.
A better idea may be to limit unhealthy choices and make healthy food easier to find.
Children need guidance, not just rules.

lessons.title: Advertising to Children Should Be Limited
lessons.topic: Advertising to Children Should Be Limited
lessons.passage:
Children see advertisements on videos, websites, games and television.
Some adverts are harmless, but young children may not always understand that the main purpose is to make people want to buy something.
This can be a problem when adverts promote unhealthy food, expensive toys or products children do not really need.
I do not think all advertising should disappear.
Families need information about products too.
However, advertising made especially for young children should be limited and clear.
Children should also learn to ask, “Do I really need this, or does the advert simply make it look exciting?”

lessons.title: Children Should Earn Some of Their Pocket Money
lessons.topic: Children Should Earn Some of Their Pocket Money
lessons.passage:
I think children can learn something useful by earning part of their pocket money.
Normal family responsibilities, such as tidying our own room, should not always be paid.
But parents could offer a small reward for extra jobs.
For example, a child might help wash the family car or organise an old cupboard.
When children earn money through effort, they may think more carefully before spending it.
They can also learn the value of saving.
Pocket money should still be simple and suitable for a child's age.
The point is not to turn home into a workplace, but to teach a useful lesson about effort and money.

lessons.title: Children Should Have Screen-Time Rules on School Nights
lessons.topic: Children Should Have Screen-Time Rules on School Nights
lessons.passage:
School nights are busy.
Children may need to finish homework, prepare their school bags, eat dinner and get enough sleep.
If phones, tablets or games take up the whole evening, other important things can be pushed aside.
That is why I think families should have simple screen-time rules on school nights.
The rule does not need to be the same for every family.
A child may use a device for homework, and some screen time for fun is fine too.
The important thing is having a limit.
Screens should fit into the evening routine, not control it.
