lessons.title: Primary School Children Are Too Young for Social Media
lessons.topic: Primary School Children Are Too Young for Social Media
lessons.passage:
Social media can be fun, but I think primary school children are usually too young to manage it alone.
Online, children may see content they do not understand, share too much personal information or communicate with people they do not know.
There can also be pressure to get likes, follow trends or compare ourselves with others.
Children can still enjoy the internet without having their own social media accounts.
They can watch suitable videos, learn online or message family with adult guidance.
For me, social media can wait.
There is no need to rush into something just because older people are using it.

lessons.title: Students Should Be Allowed to Use AI with Teacher Permission
lessons.topic: Students Should Be Allowed to Use AI with Teacher Permission
lessons.passage:
AI can help students in useful ways if it is used carefully.
A student might ask AI to explain a difficult word, give examples or suggest ideas for a project.
However, AI should not do all the work.
If students simply copy an answer, they may finish the task without learning anything.
AI can also make mistakes, so its answers should be checked.
I think students should be allowed to use AI when the teacher says it is suitable and explains how to use it responsibly.
The goal should be learning with AI, not letting AI learn in our place.

lessons.title: Video Games Can Teach Useful Skills
lessons.topic: Video Games Can Teach Useful Skills
lessons.passage:
Video games are often seen as only entertainment, but some games can teach useful skills.
Strategy games may make players plan ahead. Puzzle games can develop problem-solving, and team games can teach communication.
Some English games can even introduce new vocabulary.
That does not mean every game is educational or that children should play for hours.
The game needs to be suitable for the child's age, and playtime should have a limit.
I think video games can be one useful activity among many.
The key is choosing good games and keeping a healthy balance with study, exercise and real-life activities.

lessons.title: Tablets Should Be Used in Some School Lessons
lessons.topic: Tablets Should Be Used in Some School Lessons
lessons.passage:
Tablets can make some lessons more interesting.
Students can watch a short science video, look at a map, practise vocabulary or search for information for a project.
They can also use interactive exercises that give quick feedback.
However, tablets should not be used in every lesson.
Students still need to write by hand, read books, talk to classmates and learn without a screen.
Devices can also become a distraction if students use them for games instead of schoolwork.
I think tablets are useful when the teacher has a clear learning purpose.
Technology should support the lesson, not become the lesson itself.

lessons.title: Children Should Have Phones Only When They Really Need Them
lessons.topic: Children Should Have Phones Only When They Really Need Them
lessons.passage:
Many children want their own phones because their friends have one.
I do not think that is a strong enough reason.
A phone can be useful when a child travels to school alone, needs to contact parents or has a real reason to stay connected.
However, owning a phone also means learning to use it responsibly.
Children can easily spend too much time on games, videos or messages.
For me, the question is not “How old should a child be?” but “Does this child really need a phone, and are they ready to follow the rules?”
A phone should be a useful tool, not something we have only because everyone else does.

Children can easily spend too much time on games, videos or messages.

lessons.title: School Libraries Should Be More Fun and Welcoming
lessons.topic: School Libraries Should Be More Fun and Welcoming
lessons.passage:
A school library should be quiet enough for reading, but it does not need to feel serious or boring.
I think libraries should make children want to come inside.
They can have comfortable reading corners, interesting book displays and simple recommendations for different ages and interests.
Students might also enjoy book clubs, storytelling sessions or a “book of the month”.
The main purpose is still reading, not entertainment.
But when a library feels welcoming, children may choose to spend more time there.
A good library should make students curious about what they might discover next.

lessons.title: Students Should Use Reusable Lunch Boxes and Bottles
lessons.topic: Students Should Use Reusable Lunch Boxes and Bottles
lessons.passage:
A student may use a plastic bottle, straw, bag and food container all in one day.
That can create a lot of rubbish over a school year.
Reusable bottles and lunch boxes can help reduce some of this waste.
They can be washed and used again many times.
Of course, families should choose items that are safe, easy to clean and not too expensive.
Students also need to remember to bring them home.
It is a small change, but if many students make the same change, the amount of single-use plastic can become much smaller.

lessons.title: Every Class Should Have an Environmental Responsibility
lessons.topic: Every Class Should Have an Environmental Responsibility
lessons.passage:
Learning about the environment is useful, but students should also have chances to take action.
Each class could choose one simple responsibility.
They might remember to turn off lights and fans when they are not needed, collect paper for recycling or reduce single-use plastic.
The task should be easy enough to become a normal habit.
One classroom cannot solve every environmental problem.
Still, small actions teach children that protecting the environment is something we do, not only something we read about.

lessons.title: Students Should Help Make Some Classroom Rules
lessons.topic: Students Should Help Make Some Classroom Rules
lessons.passage:
Teachers are responsible for the classroom, so they need to set important rules.
Still, I think students can help decide some of them.
At the beginning of the year, a class could discuss questions such as how to listen respectfully, take care of materials or work well in groups.
When students help create a rule, they may understand its purpose better and feel more responsible for following it.
Of course, children cannot vote to remove every rule they dislike.
Teachers still need to make the final decisions.
But giving students a voice can help build a stronger classroom community.

lessons.title: Schools Should Teach Students How to Deal with Bullying
lessons.topic: Schools Should Teach Students How to Deal with Bullying
lessons.passage:
Students should know that bullying is not just “a normal part of school”.
If someone is repeatedly hurt, laughed at, left out or treated badly, they need support.
Schools should teach children how to recognise bullying and what to do about it.
Students can learn to tell a trusted adult, support the person being bullied and avoid joining in.
They should not be expected to solve dangerous situations alone.
A safe school is not only a place without physical danger.
It is also a place where students feel respected and know that adults will listen when there is a problem.

lessons.title: Online Safety Should Be Taught in Primary School
lessons.topic: Online Safety Should Be Taught in Primary School
lessons.passage:
Children are using the internet at younger ages, so online safety should not wait until secondary school.
Students need to know that personal information, photos and passwords should be protected.
They should also understand that people online are not always who they say they are.
If something makes a child uncomfortable or worried, they should stop and tell a trusted adult.
The aim is not to make children afraid of the internet.
The internet can be useful and enjoyable.
Good online safety simply helps children use it more carefully and confidently.

lessons.title: Children Should Learn About Money at School
lessons.topic: Children Should Learn About Money at School
lessons.passage:
Children use money in simple ways long before they become adults.
We may receive pocket money, buy school supplies or save for something we want.
That is why I think schools should teach basic money skills.
Students can learn the difference between needs and wants, how to compare prices and why saving is useful.
The lessons do not need difficult maths or business ideas.
Simple activities, such as planning how to use a small amount of money, can already teach a lot.
Knowing how to manage money is a skill everyone will need later in life.

lessons.topic: First Aid Should Be Taught at School
lessons.passage:
Children may not be able to deal with serious emergencies by themselves, but they can still learn basic first aid.
Students can learn what to do with a small cut, how to use a simple bandage and when they need to call an adult.
They can also learn an important rule: stay calm and do not make the situation worse.
These lessons should be simple and suitable for the child's age.
I think first aid belongs at school because it is a practical skill that may be useful anywhere, not only in the classroom.

lessons.title: Students Should Sometimes Sit in Groups Instead of Rows
lessons.topic: Students Should Sometimes Sit in Groups Instead of Rows
lessons.passage:
Sitting in rows can be useful when students need to listen carefully to the teacher or work quietly.
But for some activities, sitting in groups works better.
Students can look at one another, share materials and discuss ideas more easily.
This can be especially helpful for speaking activities, projects and team tasks.
Of course, group seating can become noisy if students forget to focus.
That is why I do not think one classroom arrangement is best for every lesson.
A flexible classroom can change depending on what students need to do.

lessons.title: Schools Should Use More Project-Based Learning
lessons.topic: Schools Should Use More Project-Based Learning
lessons.passage:
I think students should have more chances to learn through projects.
A project can bring different skills together. Students may need to find information, make something, work with classmates and present their ideas.
For example, a class studying the environment could create posters about reducing plastic or grow plants and record their progress.
Projects can make lessons feel more connected to real life.
However, they should not replace every normal lesson. Students still need clear teaching and individual practice.
For me, project work is most useful when it supports what students are already learning.

lessons.title: Students Should Go on More Educational Trips
lessons.topic: Students Should Go on More Educational Trips
lessons.passage:
Some lessons become much more interesting when students can see the subject in real life.
A history class may feel different after visiting a historical site. A science topic can become clearer at a museum, farm or nature centre.
Educational trips also give students a chance to learn outside their normal classroom.
Of course, trips cost money and need careful planning, so schools cannot organise them every week.
But when possible, I think students should have more opportunities to learn through real experiences.
A good trip can make a lesson much easier to remember.

lessons.title: Comfortable Uniforms Are More Important Than Formal Uniforms
lessons.topic: Comfortable Uniforms Are More Important Than Formal Uniforms
lessons.passage:
A school uniform can look smart, but students also have to wear it for many hours.
That is why comfort should come first.
In hot weather, uniforms should use light materials and allow students to move easily during lessons and break time.
A very formal uniform may look impressive, but it is not helpful if students feel hot or uncomfortable all day.
This does not mean uniforms should look untidy.
I think schools can have clothes that are both neat and practical.
For everyday school life, comfort matters more than looking extremely formal.

lessons.title: Schools Should Not Rank Young Students
lessons.topic: Schools Should Not Rank Young Students
lessons.passage:
Knowing who got the highest mark may be interesting, but I do not think young students need to be ranked all the time.
Children develop at different speeds.
One student may be strong in Maths, another may speak English confidently, and someone else may be very creative.
A class ranking can make some children proud, but it can also make others feel that they are not good enough.
I think it is more helpful to show students their own progress.
Competition can sometimes motivate us, but learning should not always be about being better than the person sitting next to us.

lessons.title: Every School Should Offer Clubs After Class
lessons.topic: Every School Should Offer Clubs After Class
lessons.passage:
Not every child discovers their interests during normal lessons.
School clubs can give students a chance to try activities such as sports, art, English, music, science or chess.
A club can also help children make friends with people who enjoy the same things.
I think schools should offer a few different clubs when they have enough teachers, space and time.
Students should not be forced to join too many activities, though.
After-school clubs are most useful when children choose them because they are genuinely interested.

lessons.title: Primary Schools Should Start a Little Later
lessons.topic: Primary Schools Should Start a Little Later
lessons.passage:
Some children have to wake up very early to get ready and travel to school.
Starting a little later could give them more time to sleep and have breakfast without rushing.
However, changing the school start time is not simple.
Parents have work schedules, traffic can be busy, and many children have activities after school.
That is why I would only suggest a small change, not a completely different timetable.
The best school start time should help children feel rested while still working well for families.

lessons.title: Homework Should Have a Time Limit
lessons.topic: Homework Should Have a Time Limit
lessons.passage:
Homework should help students practise, not take over the whole evening.
That is why I think it should have a reasonable time limit.
If a child spends hours trying to finish homework every night, there may be too much work or the task may be too difficult.
Children also need time to eat, exercise, relax and sleep.
A time limit does not mean students can stop after five minutes without trying.
It simply means schools should think about how much work is suitable for the child's age.
Good homework should be useful, not exhausting.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn How to Use Dictionaries Well
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn How to Use Dictionaries Well
lessons.passage:
When students see a new English word, they often ask the teacher for the meaning straight away.
Sometimes that is fine, but learning to use a dictionary can make us more independent.
A good dictionary can show much more than a Vietnamese meaning. It can tell us how to pronounce the word, what type of word it is and how it is used in a sentence.
Students should also learn that the first meaning is not always the right one.
Knowing how to look up words properly can save time and help us understand English more accurately.

lessons.title: Children Should Learn Debate at Primary School
lessons.topic: Children Should Learn Debate at Primary School
lessons.passage:
I think primary school children can learn simple debate skills.
Debate does not have to mean arguing loudly or trying to defeat another person.
Students can learn how to give an opinion, explain a reason and listen to a different point of view.
For example, a class might discuss whether homework should be shorter or whether students need more break time.
Children can disagree politely and still respect one another.
These skills are useful in speaking, writing and everyday communication.
Debate can also teach us that two people can think differently without becoming enemies.

lessons.title: Every Student Should Practise Speaking in Front of the Class
lessons.topic: Every Student Should Practise Speaking in Front of the Class
lessons.passage:
Standing in front of a class can feel scary, especially for shy students.
Still, I think everyone should practise it little by little.
Students can start with something small, such as introducing themselves, describing a picture or giving a one-minute talk.
The more we practise, the less frightening it often becomes.
Speaking in front of others is useful not only for school presentations but also for many situations later in life.
Teachers should not embarrass nervous students or expect everyone to speak perfectly.
The goal is to help each student become more confident step by step.

lessons.title: Teacher Feedback Is More Useful Than Grades Alone
lessons.topic: Teacher Feedback Is More Useful Than Grades Alone
lessons.passage:
A grade can tell students how well they did, but it does not always tell them what to do next.
That is why I think teacher feedback is very important.
If a teacher says, “Your ideas are good, but check your spelling,” the student knows exactly what to improve.
A number or letter alone cannot always give that information.
Grades can still be useful because they show progress over time.
But for learning, clear comments and advice may help students more.
I think the best system uses both: a grade when needed and helpful feedback to guide the next step.

lessons.title: Students Should Learn to Check Their Own Work
lessons.topic: Students Should Learn to Check Their Own Work
lessons.passage:
Many students finish an exercise and immediately say, “Teacher, is this right?”
I think we should learn to check our own work first.
We can reread a sentence, check our spelling, look at a Maths answer again or make sure we completed every question.
We will not find every mistake, and teachers are still there to help.
But checking our work teaches us to be more careful and independent.
It can also help us notice the kinds of mistakes we make often.
Learning does not end when we write the final answer. Sometimes the most useful part is looking at it one more time.

lessons.title: Art and Music Are as Important as Academic Subjects
lessons.topic: Art and Music Are as Important as Academic Subjects
lessons.passage:
Maths, Vietnamese, English and Science are important, but children develop in more than one way.
Art allows students to create and express ideas. Music gives them a chance to sing, listen and sometimes perform with others.
These subjects can help children discover talents that may not appear in a Maths test.
They can also make the school week more balanced and enjoyable.
I do not think every subject needs exactly the same number of lessons.
But art and music should not be treated as unimportant just because they are different from academic subjects.

lessons.title: Students Should Have More PE Lessons
lessons.topic: Students Should Have More PE Lessons
lessons.passage:
Students spend many hours each week sitting at desks, so I think schools should make enough time for physical activity.
PE lessons help children develop fitness, balance and coordination. Team games can also teach cooperation.
For some students, PE is one of the few chances they have to exercise regularly.
Of course, schools need time for Maths, English and other academic subjects too.
I do not think PE should replace them.
But keeping the body healthy is part of education as well.
A good school timetable should give students time to develop both their minds and their bodies.

lessons.title: Schools Should Have Quiet Reading Time Every Day
lessons.topic: Schools Should Have Quiet Reading Time Every Day
lessons.passage:
Students already read in many lessons, but quiet reading time has a different purpose.
It gives children a chance to choose a book and read simply because they are interested in it.
Some students may choose stories, while others prefer science books, comics or books about animals.
Even ten minutes of quiet reading each day can help build a strong habit.
I would not use this time for tests or worksheets.
The goal should be to help children discover that reading can be enjoyable, not only something they do because a teacher tells them to.

lessons.title: Schools Should Have a Small Garden
lessons.topic: Schools Should Have a Small Garden
lessons.passage:
A small school garden could turn part of the school grounds into a place for learning.
Students could grow flowers, herbs or simple vegetables and learn what plants need to stay healthy.
Science lessons might become more interesting when children can observe real plants instead of only looking at pictures.
A garden also teaches patience and responsibility because plants need regular care.
Of course, not every school has a lot of space.
Even a few pots or a small green corner could work.
The idea is not to build a farm, but to give students more contact with nature.

lessons.topic: Every Student Should Have a Classroom Job
lessons.passage:
A classroom works better when students help take care of it.
I think every student could have a small classroom job from time to time.
One child might hand out books, another could water the plants, and someone else could help organise learning materials.
The jobs should rotate so that everyone gets a turn.
These tasks do not need to take much time.
Their purpose is to teach students that the classroom is a shared space.
When everyone contributes a little, students can become more responsible and the class can feel more like a team.

lessons.title: Schools Should Have Longer Lunch Breaks
lessons.topic: Schools Should Have Longer Lunch Breaks
lessons.passage:
Lunch break should be more than just enough time to finish a meal quickly.
Students need time to eat properly, drink water, talk with friends and rest before afternoon lessons.
If the break is too short, children may rush their food or return to class without feeling refreshed.
However, a very long lunch break could make the school day finish later.
So I would not make it much longer.
Even an extra ten or fifteen minutes could help students enjoy their meal and return to class with more energy.

lessons.title: Students Should Not Have Tests Every Week
lessons.topic: Students Should Not Have Tests Every Week
lessons.passage:
Tests can help teachers see what students understand, so I do not think they should disappear.
But having an important test every week may create too much pressure for younger students.
Children need time to learn, practise and make mistakes before they are tested.
Teachers can also check progress through class activities, short quizzes, projects or speaking tasks.
A small quiz sometimes is fine.
The problem is when students spend too much time worrying about marks.
I think tests should support learning, not make children afraid of learning.

lessons.title: Teachers Should Use More Group Work
lessons.topic: Teachers Should Use More Group Work
lessons.passage:
Students need to learn how to work independently, but group work is important too.
In a group, students can share ideas, explain things to one another and solve a problem together.
It can be especially useful in English lessons because everyone gets more chances to speak.
However, good group work needs clear roles. If one student does everything while the others stay quiet, the activity is not very helpful.
Teachers should still use individual work as well.
For me, the best classroom has a mixture of both.

lessons.title: Students Should Have More Choice in Their Homework

lessons.passage:
Homework is useful when it helps students practise what they learned, but I think children could sometimes have more choice in how they do it.
For example, a teacher might let students choose between writing a short paragraph, making a poster or recording a short speaking task.
Students still practise the same lesson, but they can use a method that suits them better.
Of course, not every homework task can be optional.
Some exercises are necessary for everyone.
Still, having a little choice can make homework feel more interesting and encourage students to take more responsibility for their learning.

lessons.title: Families Should Have a Mostly Screen-Free Day Sometimes
lessons.topic: Families Should Have a Mostly Screen-Free Day Sometimes
lessons.passage:
Phones, tablets and televisions are part of modern family life, so I do not think we need to avoid screens completely.
But having a mostly screen-free day from time to time could be refreshing.
Families could go outside, cook together, visit relatives, play games or simply spend more time talking.
There may still be good reasons to use a phone, such as calling someone or checking important information. That is why I prefer “mostly screen-free” rather than a strict ban.
The aim is not to punish anyone.
It is simply a reminder that entertainment does not always need a screen.

lessons.title: Team Games Are Better Than Individual Games at Parties
lessons.topic: Team Games Are Better Than Individual Games at Parties
lessons.passage:
At a party, I think team games often create a better atmosphere than games where only one person can win.
In a team, children can work together, cheer for one another and share the fun.
Team games can also help shy children join in because they do not have to stand alone in front of everyone.
Of course, individual games can be exciting too.
The most important thing is that no one feels left out.
For a class party or birthday, I would choose more team activities because they help people mix, laugh and enjoy the celebration together.

lessons.title: Children Should Learn to Make Healthy Food Choices
lessons.topic: Children Should Learn to Make Healthy Food Choices
lessons.passage:
Adults usually decide what young children eat, but children should also learn how to make good food choices for themselves.
We can learn that a healthy meal does not mean eating only vegetables. Our bodies need a variety of foods, such as rice, fruit, vegetables, eggs, fish, meat or beans.
We can also learn why sugary drinks and snacks are better as occasional treats.
No food needs to be called “bad” all the time.
The goal is to understand balance.
If children learn this early, they can make better choices when they become more independent.

lessons.title: Students Should Pack Their School Bags the Night Before
lessons.topic: Students Should Pack Their School Bags the Night Before
lessons.passage:
A school morning is much easier when the bag is already packed.
Before going to bed, students can check the next day's timetable and make sure they have the right books, notebooks and school supplies.
This only takes a few minutes, but it can prevent a lot of problems.
If we wait until the morning, we may be in a hurry and forget something important.
Preparing the night before also helps us become more organised.
It is a small habit, but I think it can make school days less stressful.

lessons.title: Simple Birthday Celebrations Can Be the Best
lessons.topic: Simple Birthday Celebrations Can Be the Best
lessons.passage:
A birthday does not need a large party to feel special.
Sometimes a small celebration at home can be even more enjoyable because there is less pressure and more time to talk.
A cake, a favourite meal, a few games and people we care about may be enough.
Children can also help decorate the room or choose an activity for the day.
Big parties can be exciting, but they are not the only way to celebrate.
For me, a good birthday is about feeling loved and enjoying the people around us, not about having the biggest party.

lessons.title: Families Should Waste Less Food
lessons.passage:
Sometimes families cook too much food and a lot of it ends up in the bin.
I think we should try to waste less.
One simple idea is to take a smaller portion first and get more food if we are still hungry. Families can also keep safe leftovers for another meal instead of throwing them away.
Children should not be forced to eat when they are already full, but we can learn to take only what we need.
Food takes time, money and resources to produce.
Using it carefully is a simple way to show respect for both our family and the environment.

lessons.title: Children Should Learn Basic Cooking
lessons.passage:
I think basic cooking is a skill children can start learning step by step.
We do not need to prepare difficult dishes. We can begin with washing vegetables, making a sandwich, preparing fruit or cooking something simple with an adult.
Cooking helps children understand what goes into their food. It can also make us more confident about preparing a meal when we are older.
Safety is very important, so children should not use sharp knives, hot oil or fire without proper guidance.
Learning to cook is not only about food. It is also part of learning how to take care of ourselves.

lessons.title: Experiences Are Better Than Having More Toys
lessons.topic: Experiences Are Better Than Having More Toys
lessons.passage:
New toys are exciting, but after a while, some of them may stay in a cupboard and hardly be used.
Experiences can be different.
A family picnic, a trip to the beach, a cooking day with grandparents or a visit to a new place can create memories that stay with us for years.
Experiences also give children stories to tell and new things to discover.
Of course, toys can be fun and useful too.
But if I had to choose between another toy and a special day with my family, I would probably choose the experience.

lessons.title: Fruit Is a Better Snack Than Sweets
lessons.topic: Fruit Is a Better Snack Than Sweets
lessons.passage:
When children feel hungry between meals, it is easy to choose candy, biscuits or chocolate.
I enjoy those foods too, but I think fruit is a better everyday snack.
Vietnam has many delicious kinds of fruit, such as mangoes, bananas, dragon fruit, oranges and watermelon. They are naturally sweet and give our bodies useful vitamins.
Sweets can still be enjoyed sometimes. They do not need to disappear completely.
The important thing is what we choose most often.
For a normal school day, I would rather have fresh fruit than a bag of sweets.

lessons.title: Children Should Keep Their Rooms Tidy Without Being Reminded
lessons.topic: Children Should Keep Their Rooms Tidy Without Being Reminded
lessons.passage:
Parents should not have to remind children every day to pick up clothes, books and toys.
I think keeping our own room tidy is one way to become more responsible.
It does not mean the room has to look perfect all the time. We can simply put things back in the right place and spend a few minutes cleaning up each day.
When our room is organised, it is easier to find what we need and prepare for school.
At first, children may need reminders. But over time, tidying up should become a normal part of taking care of our own space.

lessons.title: A Good Morning Routine Makes the Day Better
lessons.topic: A Good Morning Routine Makes the Day Better
lessons.passage:
A difficult morning can make the whole day feel stressful.
If we wake up late, look for missing books and skip breakfast, we may arrive at school already tired and worried.
A simple routine can make things easier.
We can get up at a regular time, wash and dress, eat breakfast and check our school bag before leaving.
Preparing some things the night before can help too.
We do not need a perfect morning every day.
But when we are organised and do not have to rush, we can begin school feeling calmer and more ready to learn.

lessons.title: Everyone Needs Some Quiet Time
lessons.passage:
Children spend a lot of time around other people. We study with classmates, talk with family and join activities after school.
That is why I think everyone also needs a little quiet time.
Being alone for a short time does not mean feeling lonely.
We can read, draw, listen to music or simply sit and think.
Quiet time can help us relax after a noisy or busy day.
Some children need more of it than others, and that is completely fine.
Having personal space can help us feel calmer and ready to enjoy other people again.

lessons.title: Children Should Learn How to Read a Map
lessons.topic: Children Should Learn How to Read a Map
lessons.passage:
Today, people often use phones to find directions, so reading a paper map may seem unnecessary.
I still think children should understand basic maps.
Maps teach us about directions, locations, routes and symbols. They can help us understand where places are instead of simply following a screen.
For example, students can learn to read a simple map of their school, neighbourhood or a tourist attraction.
Phones are very useful for navigation, but technology does not always work perfectly.
Knowing how a map works is still a useful skill.

lessons.title: Older Children Should Help Younger Brothers and Sisters
lessons.topic: Older Children Should Help Younger Brothers and Sisters
lessons.passage:
Older brothers and sisters can be important people in a child's life.
They can help younger children with simple homework, show them how to do something or keep them company when parents are busy.
Older children can also set a good example by being kind and responsible.
However, I do not think they should become a second parent.
They still need time for their own schoolwork, friends and hobbies.
Helping younger siblings is a good family habit, but the responsibility should stay reasonable.

lessons.title: Having a Pet Can Teach Responsibility
lessons.topic: Having a Pet Can Teach Responsibility
lessons.passage:
A pet can be fun to play with, but owning an animal also means having responsibilities.
Dogs, cats, fish and other pets need food, clean water and proper care every day.
Children can help with these jobs and learn that another living thing depends on them.
This can build good habits because pet care cannot simply be forgotten when we feel busy.
However, parents still need to make sure the animal is treated properly.
A pet should never be bought only to teach a lesson.
If a family is ready, caring for an animal can be a meaningful way for children to learn responsibility.

lessons.topic: Family Trips Are Better Than Expensive Gifts
lessons.passage:
A new toy or an expensive gift can be exciting, but the excitement may not last forever.
A family trip can give us memories that stay much longer.
The trip does not need to be far away. A day at the beach, a visit to a museum or a picnic in a nearby place can still be special.
During a trip, family members talk, explore and experience something together.
I like receiving gifts too, but if I had to choose, I would prefer a good day out with my family.
Memories are difficult to put in a box, but they can last for years.

lessons.topic: Children Should Choose Some of the Books They Read
lessons.passage:
Teachers and parents can introduce children to good books, but I think young readers should have some choice too.
One child may love adventure stories, while another prefers science, animals or funny comics.
When students choose a book that interests them, they are often more willing to read.
Of course, adults can still help by recommending books that are suitable for the child's age and reading level.
For me, the best reading habit comes from both guidance and choice.
Children need good books, but they also need the freedom to discover what they enjoy.

lessons.title: It Is Better to Have One Hobby You Love Than Many Hobbies
lessons.topic: It Is Better to Have One Hobby You Love Than Many Hobbies
lessons.passage:
Trying different hobbies is a good way to discover what we enjoy.
But after some time, I think it is useful to have one activity that we really love and want to improve.
When we focus on one hobby, we can practise more often and notice our progress.
For example, a child who enjoys badminton may become better by playing regularly instead of changing activities every week.
This does not mean we can only have one interest.
We can enjoy many things, but having one favourite hobby can give us something special to work towards.

lessons.title: Listening to Music Can Make Study Time Better
lessons.topic: Listening to Music Can Make Study Time Better
lessons.passage:
Some students enjoy complete silence when they study. Others prefer a little music in the background.
For me, soft music can make study time more relaxing, especially when I am drawing, organising notes or doing simple exercises.
However, music with loud sounds or lyrics can sometimes distract us. We may start singing instead of working.
So I do not think music is helpful for every task.
The best choice depends on the student and the type of work.
If music helps us concentrate, we can keep the volume low and use it wisely.

lessons.title: Keeping a Diary Is Good for Children
lessons.topic: Keeping a Diary Is Good for Children
lessons.passage:
Keeping a diary may sound old-fashioned, but I think it can be a very good habit for children.
We can write about something funny that happened at school, a trip with our family or how we felt after a difficult day.
Writing helps us remember small moments that we may forget later. It can also help us understand our feelings better.
For students learning English, a short English diary can even be useful writing practice.
A diary does not need to be long. Just a few sentences from time to time can become a special record of our childhood.

lessons.title: Children Should Spend Part of Every Weekend Outdoors
lessons.topic: Children Should Spend Part of Every Weekend Outdoors
lessons.passage:
Weekends are often the best time to rest after a busy school week. Resting does not have to mean staying indoors all day.
I think children should spend at least some weekend time outside when the weather is suitable.
We can ride bikes, play badminton, visit a park, walk with our family or simply explore our neighbourhood.
Outdoor time gives us fresh air and helps us stay active.
Of course, children also need time for homework and quiet activities at home.
For me, a good weekend has a balance: some study, some rest and some time outside.

lessons.title: Walking or Cycling Is Better for Short Trips
lessons.topic: Walking or Cycling Is Better for Short Trips
lessons.passage:
For a short trip, I think walking or cycling can be better than using a motorbike or car.
It gives us some exercise and does not create pollution while we travel.
For example, if a park or shop is close to home, walking there can be part of the activity instead of just a way to get there.
However, safety comes first. Some roads are very busy, and children should not cycle alone in unsafe traffic.
So I would choose walking or cycling only when the distance is reasonable and the route is safe.

lessons.title: Homemade Food Is Better Than Fast Food
lessons.topic: Homemade Food Is Better Than Fast Food
lessons.passage:
Fast food is convenient and can be very tasty. I enjoy it sometimes, especially when my family is busy or when we go out together.
For everyday meals, though, I prefer homemade food.
At home, families can choose fresh ingredients and prepare dishes in a way that suits them. A normal Vietnamese meal with rice, vegetables, soup and meat or fish can give us different kinds of food in one meal.
Home cooking also gives family members a chance to eat together.
Fast food can still be a treat, but I would not want it to replace home-cooked meals.

lessons.title: Saving Money Is Better Than Buying Small Treats
lessons.topic: Saving Money Is Better Than Buying Small Treats
lessons.passage:
It can be tempting to spend pocket money as soon as we get it.
A snack, a toy or a small game may not cost much, but buying little things again and again can use all our money very quickly.
I think saving at least part of our money is a better habit.
If we have a goal, such as buying a book or something useful, saving teaches us to wait and plan.
This does not mean we can never buy a treat. Spending a little can be enjoyable too.
The important thing is learning that we do not have to buy something every time we have money.

lessons.title: Birthday Parties Do Not Need to Be Expensive
lessons.topic: Birthday Parties Do Not Need to Be Expensive
lessons.passage:
A birthday is special, but I do not think families need to spend a lot of money to make it memorable.
Children often remember the people and the fun more than expensive decorations. A small cake, a few friends and some simple games can make a wonderful party.
Families can even celebrate at home instead of going somewhere expensive.
Of course, there is nothing wrong with having a bigger party when a family wants one.
But children should not feel that a great birthday depends on how much money is spent.
For me, being with people who care about us is what makes the day meaningful.

lessons.title: Every Child Should Learn One Useful Household Skill
lessons.topic: Every Child Should Learn One Useful Household Skill
lessons.passage:
School teaches us many important subjects, but children also need practical skills for everyday life.
I think every child should learn at least one household skill well. It could be preparing a simple breakfast, folding clothes, organising a study area or helping with laundry.
These jobs may seem small, but they help children become more independent.
When we know how to take care of simple things ourselves, we do not always need to wait for an adult to help us.
As we get older, we can learn more. A few useful skills at a young age are a very good start.

lessons.title: Hobbies Are Better Than Extra Screen Time
lessons.topic: Hobbies Are Better Than Extra Screen Time
lessons.passage:
After homework, it is easy to pick up a phone or tablet and spend the rest of the evening on a screen.
I think having a hobby is a better choice.
A hobby gives us something to practise and improve. We might draw, play badminton, build models, dance, read or learn an instrument. Some hobbies keep us active, while others help us become more creative.
Screens can also be useful and entertaining, so I do not think children need to avoid them completely.
However, if all our free time goes to videos and games, we may never discover something else we are good at.

lessons.title: Families Should Eat Dinner Together More Often
lessons.topic: Families Should Eat Dinner Together More Often
lessons.passage:
It is not always easy for families to eat together. Parents may finish work late, and children may have classes or other activities.
Still, I think family dinners are worth making time for.
A meal gives everyone a simple chance to sit down and talk. Children can tell their parents what happened at school, and parents can share something about their day too.
The food does not need to be special. Even a simple home-cooked meal can become important when people enjoy it together.
Families may not manage this every evening, but I think eating together several times a week is a very good habit.

lessons.title: Children Should Have Daily Chores
lessons.passage:
I think children should have one or two simple jobs to do at home each day.
These jobs do not need to be difficult. A child can make the bed, put clothes away, set the table or help tidy the living room.
When everyone helps, parents do not have to do everything alone. Children also learn that being part of a family means sharing responsibilities.
At first, parents may need to remind us. After some time, the job can become part of our daily routine.
I do not think housework should take away all our free time. But doing a small share every day is fair and useful.

lessons.title: Reading Before Bed Is Better Than Watching Videos
lessons.topic: Reading Before Bed Is Better Than Watching Videos
lessons.passage:
At the end of the day, many children like watching short videos or cartoons before going to sleep. I understand why, but I would choose a book instead.
Reading gives our minds a chance to slow down. A good story can take us to another place without a bright screen in front of our eyes. It also helps us build vocabulary and imagination.
I especially like reading for ten or fifteen minutes when I am already in bed. It feels quiet and peaceful.
Videos are fun, but they can easily turn ten minutes into an hour. For me, a book is a better way to finish the day.

lessons.title: Lesson 50: Saving Endangered Species
lessons.passage: A species becomes endangered when its population is so small that it faces a high risk of extinction. Major causes include habitat loss, pollution, climate change, and poaching. Conservation programmes may protect breeding areas, rescue injured animals, restore habitats, and enforce wildlife laws. Zoos can support research and carefully managed breeding, but animals also need safe natural environments. Consumers should avoid products made from threatened wildlife and report illegal trade. Saving endangered species is important because each species contributes to biodiversity and ecosystem stability. Prevention is usually more effective and less costly than trying to recover a species at the last moment.

exercise.translation: Một loài trở nên nguy cấp khi số lượng cá thể ít đến mức có nguy cơ tuyệt chủng cao. Nguyên nhân chính gồm mất môi trường sống, ô nhiễm, biến đổi khí hậu và săn bắt trái phép. Chương trình bảo tồn có thể bảo vệ khu sinh sản, cứu động vật bị thương, phục hồi sinh cảnh và thực thi luật về động vật hoang dã. Vườn thú có thể hỗ trợ nghiên cứu và nhân giống có quản lý, nhưng động vật vẫn cần môi trường tự nhiên an toàn. Người tiêu dùng nên tránh sản phẩm làm từ động vật bị đe dọa và báo cáo buôn bán trái phép. Bảo vệ loài nguy cấp quan trọng vì mỗi loài đóng góp cho đa dạng sinh học và ổn định hệ sinh thái. Phòng ngừa thường hiệu quả hơn cứu loài vào phút cuối. lessons.title: Lesson 49: Wetlands and River Deltas
lessons.passage: Wetlands and river deltas are valuable ecosystems between land and water. They provide habitats for fish, birds, plants, and many small organisms. Wetlands can store freshwater, filter pollution, and reduce the impact of floods. In coastal areas, mangrove forests protect the land from waves and create nursery grounds for young fish. Yet these ecosystems may be damaged by construction, waste, overuse of water, and climate change. Protecting wetlands requires careful land-use planning and cooperation with local communities. A healthy delta supports biodiversity, farming, fishing, and the safety of millions of people.

exercise.translation:
Vùng đất ngập nước và đồng bằng sông là hệ sinh thái có giá trị nằm giữa đất và nước. Chúng cung cấp môi trường sống cho cá, chim, thực vật và nhiều sinh vật nhỏ. Đất ngập nước có thể lưu trữ nước ngọt, lọc ô nhiễm và giảm tác động của lũ. Ở vùng ven biển, rừng ngập mặn bảo vệ đất khỏi sóng và tạo nơi sinh trưởng cho cá non. Tuy vậy, các hệ sinh thái này có thể bị hư hại bởi xây dựng, rác thải, khai thác nước quá mức và biến đổi khí hậu. Bảo vệ đất ngập nước cần quy hoạch sử dụng đất cẩn thận và hợp tác với cộng đồng địa phương. Một đồng bằng khỏe mạnh hỗ trợ đa dạng sinh học, nông nghiệp, nghề cá và an toàn của hàng triệu người.

lessons.title: Lesson 48: Protecting Coral Reefs
lessons.passage: Coral reefs are rich marine ecosystems that provide food and shelter for many sea species. They also protect coastal areas from waves and support fishing and tourism. However, reefs are threatened by warmer oceans, pollution, destructive fishing, and overfishing. Plastic waste and chemicals can damage coral, while careless tourists may break it by touching or standing on it. Conservation measures include protected marine areas, responsible tourism, cleaner water, and sustainable fishing rules. People living far from the coast can also help by reducing plastic waste and carbon emissions. Healthy coral reefs benefit both nature and human communities.

exercise.translation:
Rạn san hô là hệ sinh thái biển phong phú, cung cấp thức ăn và nơi trú ẩn cho nhiều loài. Chúng còn bảo vệ vùng ven biển khỏi sóng và hỗ trợ nghề cá, du lịch. Tuy nhiên, rạn san hô bị đe dọa bởi đại dương ấm lên, ô nhiễm, đánh bắt hủy diệt và khai thác quá mức. Rác nhựa, hóa chất làm hỏng san hô, còn du khách thiếu ý thức có thể bẻ gãy khi chạm hoặc giẫm lên. Biện pháp bảo tồn gồm khu bảo vệ biển, du lịch có trách nhiệm, nước sạch hơn và quy định đánh bắt bền vững. Người sống xa biển cũng có thể giúp bằng cách giảm rác nhựa và khí thải carbon. Rạn san hô khỏe mạnh có lợi cho thiên nhiên và cộng đồng.

lessons.title: Lesson 47: The Importance of Rainforests
lessons.passage: Rainforests contain extraordinary biodiversity and provide habitats for countless species. Their trees store carbon, influence rainfall, protect soil, and support local communities. Scientists also study rainforest plants because they may contain useful substances for medicine. However, logging, farming, mining, and roads can destroy large areas of forest. Conservation should protect both wildlife and the rights of people who depend on the forest. Governments can create protected areas, control illegal activities, and support sustainable livelihoods. Saving rainforests is not only about distant animals; it helps regulate the global environment on which everyone depends.

Rừng mưa có đa dạng sinh học đặc biệt và cung cấp nơi sống cho vô số loài. Cây rừng lưu trữ carbon, ảnh hưởng lượng mưa, bảo vệ đất và hỗ trợ cộng đồng địa phương. Bảo tồn cần bảo vệ cả động vật hoang dã và quyền của những người phụ thuộc vào rừng. Chính phủ có thể lập khu bảo vệ, kiểm soát hoạt động trái phép và hỗ trợ sinh kế bền vững. Cứu rừng mưa không chỉ vì động vật ở xa mà còn giúp điều hòa môi trường toàn cầu.

lessons.title: Lesson 45: Mental Health Awareness at School
lessons.passage: Many students experience anxiety because of exams, relationships, family problems, or uncertainty about the future. Some may also experience depression and need professional support. A school mental health campaign can teach students to recognise warning signs, manage stress, and ask for help early. It should make clear that admitting a difficulty is not a weakness. Teachers need training, and students need confidential ways to contact a counsellor or trusted adult. Friends can listen and encourage support, but they should not try to diagnose or treat serious conditions. A caring school culture helps every student feel safer and less alone.

Chiến dịch sức khỏe tinh thần trong trường có thể dạy học sinh nhận biết dấu hiệu cảnh báo, quản lý căng thẳng và tìm giúp đỡ sớm. Chiến dịch cần khẳng định việc thừa nhận khó khăn không phải là yếu đuối. Giáo viên cần được tập huấn, còn học sinh cần cách liên hệ bảo mật với tư vấn viên hoặc người lớn đáng tin cậy. lessons.title: Lesson 44: Overpopulation in Big Cities
lessons.passage: Overpopulation can place heavy pressure on big cities. When the population grows faster than infrastructure, there may be shortages of housing, schools, hospitals, and clean water. Traffic becomes crowded, waste increases, and pollution may get worse. Building more roads alone is not a complete solution. Cities need better public transport, affordable housing, efficient public services, and development opportunities in smaller towns and rural areas. Family education and access to health services are also important. The goal is not to blame people for living in cities, but to plan population growth fairly and sustainably.

exercise.translation:
Quá tải dân số có thể gây áp lực lớn lên các thành phố. Khi dân số tăng nhanh hơn cơ sở hạ tầng, có thể thiếu nhà ở, trường học, bệnh viện và nước sạch. Giao thông đông đúc, rác tăng và ô nhiễm nghiêm trọng hơn. Chỉ xây thêm đường không phải giải pháp hoàn chỉnh. Thành phố cần giao thông công cộng tốt hơn, nhà ở vừa túi tiền, dịch vụ công hiệu quả và cơ hội phát triển tại thị trấn nhỏ, vùng nông thôn. Giáo dục gia đình và khả năng tiếp cận dịch vụ y tế cũng quan trọng. Mục tiêu không phải đổ lỗi cho người sống ở thành phố mà là quy hoạch tăng trưởng dân số công bằng và bền vững.

lessons.title: Lesson 43: Poverty and Community Support
lessons.passage: Poverty affects people's access to food, housing, health care, and education. Some families may become homeless or struggle to meet basic needs. Charity can provide urgent support, such as meals, clothes, or temporary shelter. However, long-term solutions should also create opportunities through education, job training, affordable housing, and fair employment. When students volunteer, they should respect people's dignity and avoid treating poverty as entertainment. Community projects work best when they listen to the people they aim to support. Social problems are complex, but informed and respectful action can make a real difference.

Khi tình nguyện, học sinh nên tôn trọng phẩm giá và không biến nghèo đói thành nội dung giải trí. Dự án cộng đồng hiệu quả nhất khi lắng nghe người cần hỗ trợ. Vấn đề xã hội phức tạp, nhưng hành động có hiểu biết và tôn trọng có thể tạo khác biệt thật sự.

lessons.title: Lesson 42: Dealing with Peer Pressure
lessons.passage: Peer pressure happens when friends influence someone to behave in a certain way. It can be positive, such as encouraging study or sport, but it can also involve alcohol, drugs, dangerous driving, or dishonest behaviour. When hanging out with friends, teenagers may fear being rejected if they refuse. A useful response is to say no clearly, give a short reason, and leave an unsafe situation. We should think about consequences before acting and choose friends who respect our limits. Asking a parent, teacher, or counsellor for support is a sensible decision when pressure becomes difficult to manage.

exercise.title: Lesson 42: Dealing with Peer Pressure

sentences.text: Peer pressure happens when friends influence someone to behave in a certain way.
It can be positive, such as encouraging study or sport, but it can also involve alcohol, drugs, dangerous driving, or dishonest behaviour.
When hanging out with friends, teenagers may fear being rejected if they refuse.
A useful response is to say no clearly, give a short reason, and leave an unsafe situation.
We should think about consequences before acting and choose friends who respect our limits.
Asking a parent, teacher, or counsellor for support is a sensible decision when pressure becomes difficult to manage.

exercise.translation:
Áp lực bạn bè xảy ra khi bạn bè tác động khiến một người cư xử theo cách nhất định. Áp lực có thể tích cực, chẳng hạn khuyến khích học tập hoặc thể thao, nhưng cũng có thể liên quan đến rượu bia, ma túy, lái xe nguy hiểm hoặc hành vi không trung thực. Khi đi chơi cùng bạn, thanh thiếu niên có thể sợ bị từ chối nếu nói không. Cách phản ứng hữu ích là từ chối rõ ràng, nêu lý do ngắn và rời khỏi tình huống không an toàn. Chúng ta nên nghĩ về hậu quả trước khi hành động và chọn bạn tôn trọng giới hạn. Xin hỗ trợ từ bố mẹ, giáo viên hoặc tư vấn viên là quyết định hợp lý khi áp lực trở nên khó kiểm soát.
ENGLISH DICTATION PRACTICE • IMPORT READY

lessons.title: Lesson 40: Practical Skills for Daily Life
lessons.passage: Independence also requires practical life skills. Teenagers should learn to cook a few simple meals, wash clothes, clean their room, and share household chores. They need to get around safely by reading maps, using public transport, and planning travel time. Basic knowledge about first aid and emergency contacts is also useful. These skills combine confidence with responsibility because our decisions affect other people. Parents can guide teenagers at first, then gradually allow them to complete tasks alone. Practising daily skills at home is one of the safest ways to prepare for adult life.

lessons.title: Lesson 39: Becoming an Independent Learner
lessons.passage: An independent learner takes an active role in education. At the beginning of each month, I set a clear learning goal, such as improving vocabulary or completing a reading book. Then I choose suitable resources and carry out a simple study plan. During self-study, I take notes, check my understanding, and ask questions when necessary. I also review my progress instead of waiting only for test results. Independent learning requires discipline, but it also gives students more control. When we achieve a small goal through our own effort, we become more confident and better prepared for university and future work.

exercise.translation:
Người học tự chủ giữ vai trò tích cực trong việc học. Đầu mỗi tháng, em đặt mục tiêu rõ ràng như cải thiện từ vựng hoặc hoàn thành một cuốn sách đọc. Sau đó, em chọn nguồn phù hợp và thực hiện kế hoạch học đơn giản. Trong lúc tự học, em ghi chép, kiểm tra mức độ hiểu và đặt câu hỏi khi cần. Em cũng xem lại tiến bộ thay vì chỉ chờ kết quả kiểm tra. Học độc lập đòi hỏi kỷ luật nhưng giúp học sinh kiểm soát việc học nhiều hơn. Khi đạt một mục tiêu nhỏ bằng nỗ lực của mình, chúng ta tự tin hơn và chuẩn bị tốt hơn cho đại học, công việc tương lai.

lessons.title: Lesson 38: Decision-Making and Problem-Solving
lessons.passage: Independent people need strong decision-making skills. When I face a problem, I first define it clearly and collect relevant information. Next, I come up with several options instead of choosing the first idea. I compare possible benefits, risks, and consequences, then select the most suitable solution. If the problem is serious, asking for advice is responsible, not weak. After acting, I evaluate the result and learn from mistakes. This process helps me deal with difficulties calmly and builds confidence. Independence does not mean knowing every answer; it means taking responsibility for thoughtful choices and improving through experience.

exercise.translation:
Người tự lập cần kỹ năng ra quyết định tốt. Khi gặp vấn đề, em xác định rõ vấn đề và thu thập thông tin liên quan. Tiếp theo, em nghĩ ra nhiều phương án thay vì chọn ý tưởng đầu tiên. Em so sánh lợi ích, rủi ro và hậu quả rồi chọn giải pháp phù hợp nhất. Nếu vấn đề nghiêm trọng, xin lời khuyên là hành động có trách nhiệm chứ không phải yếu đuối. Sau khi thực hiện, em đánh giá kết quả và học từ sai lầm. Quy trình này giúp em đối phó khó khăn bình tĩnh và xây dựng tự tin. Tự lập không có nghĩa biết mọi câu trả lời mà là chịu trách nhiệm cho lựa chọn có suy nghĩ và tiến bộ qua trải nghiệm.
ENGLISH DICTATION PRACTICE • IMPORT READY

lessons.title: Lesson 37: Managing Personal Money
lessons.passage: Money management is an important part of independence. Even with a small allowance, teenagers can learn to make a budget. First, we should record our income and regular expenses. Then we can separate needs, such as school supplies and transport, from wants, such as snacks or entertainment. Saving a small amount every week helps us prepare for future goals and unexpected costs. We should compare prices and avoid buying something only because it is popular online. Responsible money management is not about never enjoying ourselves. It is about understanding limits, planning ahead, and accepting the consequences of our choices.

exercise.translation:
Quản lý tiền là phần quan trọng của sự tự lập. Ngay cả với khoản tiền tiêu vặt nhỏ, thanh thiếu niên vẫn có thể học lập ngân sách. Trước tiên, chúng ta ghi lại thu nhập và các khoản chi thường xuyên. Sau đó, phân biệt nhu cầu như đồ dùng học tập, đi lại với mong muốn như đồ ăn vặt hoặc giải trí. Tiết kiệm một khoản nhỏ mỗi tuần giúp chuẩn bị cho mục tiêu tương lai và chi phí bất ngờ. Chúng ta nên so sánh giá và tránh mua chỉ vì món đồ phổ biến trên mạng. Quản lý tiền có trách nhiệm không có nghĩa không bao giờ tận hưởng, mà là hiểu giới hạn, lên kế hoạch và chấp nhận hậu quả lựa chọn.
ENGLISH DICTATION PRACTICE • IMPORT READY

lessons.title: Lesson 35: Education Is a Lifelong Journey
lessons.passage: Education does not end when a person earns a certificate or degree. Technology and workplaces change quickly, so adults need lifelong learning to update their knowledge and skills. Some people take short online courses, while others return to university for postgraduate study, a master's degree, or a doctorate. Learning can also happen through books, professional training, volunteering, and daily experience. The best education path is therefore flexible. School-leavers should choose a useful starting point and remain ready to learn throughout their career. Curiosity and the ability to learn independently may become as important as any single qualification.

exercise.translation:
Giáo dục không kết thúc khi một người nhận chứng chỉ hoặc bằng cấp. Công nghệ và nơi làm việc thay đổi nhanh nên người lớn cần học tập suốt đời để cập nhật kiến thức, kỹ năng. Một số người học khóa trực tuyến ngắn, trong khi người khác quay lại đại học để học sau đại học, thạc sĩ hoặc tiến sĩ. Việc học cũng diễn ra qua sách, đào tạo nghề nghiệp, hoạt động tình nguyện và kinh nghiệm hằng ngày. Vì vậy, con đường giáo dục tốt nhất cần linh hoạt. Học sinh tốt nghiệp nên chọn điểm khởi đầu hữu ích và luôn sẵn sàng học trong suốt sự nghiệp. Sự tò mò và khả năng tự học có thể quan trọng ngang với bất kỳ bằng cấp riêng lẻ nào.
ENGLISH DICTATION PRACTICE • IMPORT READY

lessons.title: Lesson 34: How to Choose an Education Path
lessons.topic: How to Choose an Education Path
lessons.passage: Choosing an education path can be difficult because school-leavers have many options. The first step is to identify personal strengths, interests, and preferred working styles. Students can speak to teachers, parents, graduates, or a career adviser. They should read each programme brochure carefully and compare entry requirements, learning methods, costs, and future jobs. It is also useful to visit campuses or training centres. No choice is completely risk-free, but a decision based on reliable information is better than one based on popularity. Students can change direction later, so the goal is to choose a suitable next step, not a perfect lifetime plan.

Lựa chọn con đường giáo dục có thể khó vì học sinh tốt nghiệp có nhiều phương án. Bước đầu tiên là xác định điểm mạnh, sở thích và cách làm việc phù hợp. Học sinh có thể trao đổi với giáo viên, bố mẹ, người đã tốt nghiệp hoặc chuyên viên hướng nghiệp. Các bạn nên đọc kỹ tờ giới thiệu chương trình và so sánh yêu cầu đầu vào, phương pháp học, chi phí và công việc tương lai. Việc tham quan trường hoặc trung tâm đào tạo cũng hữu ích. Không lựa chọn nào hoàn toàn không có rủi ro, nhưng quyết định dựa trên thông tin đáng tin cậy tốt hơn quyết định theo số đông. Học sinh vẫn có thể đổi hướng sau này; mục tiêu là chọn bước tiếp theo phù hợp.

lessons.title: Lesson 33: Taking a Gap Year
lessons.passage: Some school-leavers take a gap year before continuing their education. During this time, they may volunteer, work part-time, travel, or complete an internship. A well-planned gap year can provide useful experience, improve confidence, and help students understand their interests. However, it should not become an unplanned break with no learning goal. Students need a budget, a clear schedule, and safe activities. They should also check how the gap year affects university applications. In my opinion, a gap year is valuable when it develops responsibility and gives a young person better information for the next decision.

Một năm được lên kế hoạch tốt có thể mang lại kinh nghiệm hữu ích, tăng tự tin và giúp học sinh hiểu sở thích của mình. Tuy nhiên, nó không nên trở thành kỳ nghỉ không mục tiêu. Học sinh cần ngân sách, lịch trình rõ ràng và hoạt động an toàn. Các bạn cũng nên kiểm tra việc nghỉ một năm ảnh hưởng thế nào đến hồ sơ đại học. Theo em, một năm trải nghiệm có giá trị khi phát triển trách nhiệm và cung cấp thông tin tốt hơn cho quyết định tiếp theo.

lessons.title: Lesson 32: Vocational Education and Apprenticeships
lessons.passage: Vocational education is a practical option for students who want job-specific skills. A vocational course may combine classroom learning with hands-on practice in areas such as technology, tourism, cooking, construction, or health care. An apprenticeship allows a learner to train in a real workplace while receiving guidance from experienced workers. These programmes can lead to a certificate and earlier employment. They are not less valuable than academic education; they simply serve different goals. Students should compare training quality, safety, costs, and employment prospects before applying. Skilled workers make an essential contribution to every modern economy.

lessons.title: Lesson 30: A Youth Heritage Project
lessons.passage: My proposed youth heritage project is to document an old community house. Student volunteers would interview local residents, photograph important details, and create a bilingual website about its history. We could raise awareness through social media and organise a small exhibition at school. If repairs were needed, the community might use crowdfunding to support professional restoration. Students should not attempt to restore valuable objects themselves because incorrect methods can cause damage. The project's main purpose is to connect young people with local heritage and provide accurate information. When a community understands a site's value, it is more likely to protect it.

Chúng em có thể nâng cao nhận thức qua mạng xã hội và tổ chức triển lãm nhỏ tại trường. Nếu cần sửa chữa, cộng đồng có thể huy động vốn cộng đồng để hỗ trợ việc phục hồi chuyên nghiệp. lessons.title: Lesson 29: Tourism and Heritage Protection
lessons.passage: Tourism can provide money for heritage conservation and create jobs for local people. However, too many visitors may damage buildings, leave rubbish, or disturb traditional life. Heritage tourism must therefore be sustainable. Sites can limit visitor numbers, provide clear paths, train local guides, and use entrance fees for maintenance. People who break important rules may receive a fine, but education is also necessary. Visitors should understand that a heritage site is not only a background for photos. It belongs to the community and to future generations. Responsible tourism protects both cultural value and local livelihoods.

lessons.title: Lesson 28: Preserving Intangible Cultural Heritage
lessons.passage: Not all heritage can be seen in a museum. Intangible heritage includes folk songs, traditional performances, local knowledge, rituals, and craft skills. These practices survive only when people continue to perform, teach, and pass them down. Schools can invite artisans to demonstrate their work, organise folk music clubs, or record interviews with older community members. Festive events can attract attention, but preservation should continue throughout the year. Young people do not have to copy every tradition exactly. They can learn its meaning and find respectful ways to introduce it to new audiences.

lessons.title: Lesson 25: A School Climate Campaign
lessons.passage: Our school could organise a climate campaign called One Week, Less Carbon. Students would design leaflets explaining how human activity produces pollutants and greenhouse gases. Each class could choose one practical solution, such as saving electricity, reducing food waste, or travelling to school in greener ways. We could measure results before and after the campaign and share them at an assembly. The project should focus on awareness and realistic action, not fear. It would also teach students to cooperate, collect information, and communicate clearly. A successful campaign makes environmental responsibility part of normal school life rather than a one-time event.

Mỗi lớp chọn một giải pháp thực tế như tiết kiệm điện, giảm lãng phí thức ăn hoặc đi học bằng phương tiện xanh hơn. Chúng em có thể đo kết quả trước và sau chiến dịch rồi chia sẻ trong buổi sinh hoạt. Dự án nên tập trung vào nâng cao nhận thức và hành động thực tế, không gây sợ hãi. Hoạt động còn dạy học sinh hợp tác, thu thập thông tin và giao tiếp rõ ràng. Một chiến dịch thành công biến trách nhiệm môi trường thành một phần của đời sống học đường.
ENGLISH DICTATION PRACTICE • IMPORT READY

lessons.title: Lesson 24: How Students Can Reduce Emissions
lessons.passage: Students cannot solve global warming alone, but our daily choices still matter. We can reduce emissions by walking, cycling, or using public transport when possible. At home and school, we should switch off unused lights, use energy-saving devices, and avoid wasting water. We can reuse notebooks and bags, recycle suitable materials, and refuse unnecessary single-use plastic. Eating local food and reducing food waste also help. The most important thing is to develop consistent habits rather than perform one action for a few days. When many students make small responsible choices, they influence their families and create a stronger environmental culture.

exercise.translation:
Học sinh không thể tự giải quyết sự nóng lên toàn cầu, nhưng lựa chọn hằng ngày vẫn có ý nghĩa. Chúng ta có thể giảm khí thải bằng cách đi bộ, đạp xe hoặc sử dụng giao thông công cộng khi có thể. Ở nhà và trường, chúng ta nên tắt đèn không dùng, sử dụng thiết bị tiết kiệm năng lượng và tránh lãng phí nước. Chúng ta có thể tái sử dụng vở, túi, tái chế vật liệu phù hợp và từ chối đồ nhựa dùng một lần không cần thiết. Ăn thực phẩm địa phương và giảm lãng phí thức ăn cũng hữu ích. Điều quan trọng nhất là tạo thói quen bền vững thay vì chỉ hành động vài ngày. Nhiều lựa chọn nhỏ có trách nhiệm sẽ tạo nên văn hóa môi trường mạnh hơn.

lessons.title: Lesson 23: Deforestation and Climate Change
lessons.passage: Forests play an important role in maintaining the Earth's natural balance. Trees absorb carbon dioxide, so forests act as major carbon sinks. When people cut down large areas of forest for farming, roads, or buildings, more carbon remains in the atmosphere. Deforestation also destroys wildlife habitats and reduces biodiversity. To address this problem, governments should protect natural forests, control illegal logging, and support sustainable farming. Communities can plant native trees, but planting alone cannot replace an ancient forest. Protecting existing forests is usually more effective. Climate action and forest conservation must therefore be planned together.

Rừng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc duy trì cân bằng tự nhiên của Trái Đất. Cây hấp thụ khí carbon dioxide nên rừng là những bể chứa carbon lớn. Khi con người chặt phá diện tích rừng rộng để làm nông nghiệp, đường sá hoặc xây dựng, nhiều carbon hơn tồn tại trong khí quyển. Phá rừng cũng hủy hoại nơi sống của động vật hoang dã và làm giảm đa dạng sinh học. Để giải quyết vấn đề, chính phủ cần bảo vệ rừng tự nhiên, kiểm soát khai thác gỗ trái phép và hỗ trợ nông nghiệp bền vững. Cộng đồng có thể trồng cây bản địa, nhưng trồng cây không thể thay thế hoàn toàn rừng cổ. Vì vậy, hành động khí hậu và bảo tồn rừng phải được lên kế hoạch cùng nhau.

lessons.title: Lesson 22: Consequences of a Warmer Planet
lessons.passage: Global warming has serious consequences for nature and human life. Higher temperatures melt ice and raise sea levels, which threaten coastal communities. Extreme weather events may become more frequent or severe. Some areas experience long droughts, while others face heavy rain and floods. These changes have a strong impact on farming, water supplies, health, and biodiversity. Poor communities are often the most vulnerable because they have fewer resources to recover. Climate change is not only a future problem; its effects are already visible. Therefore, governments, businesses, and individuals must act early to reduce damage and prepare for unavoidable changes.

Các hiện tượng thời tiết cực đoan có thể xảy ra thường xuyên hoặc dữ dội hơn. Một số nơi trải qua hạn hán kéo dài, nơi khác đối mặt với mưa lớn và lũ lụt. Những thay đổi này tác động mạnh đến nông nghiệp, nguồn nước, sức khỏe và đa dạng sinh học. Cộng đồng nghèo thường dễ bị tổn thương nhất vì ít nguồn lực phục hồi. Biến đổi khí hậu không chỉ là vấn đề tương lai; tác động của nó đã hiện rõ. Vì vậy, chính phủ, doanh nghiệp và cá nhân phải hành động sớm.

lessons.title: Lesson 20: ASEAN Cooperation for a Better Future
lessons.topic: ASEAN Cooperation for a Better Future
lessons.passage: No ASEAN country can solve every regional issue alone. Natural disasters, air pollution, disease, and economic difficulties can affect several countries at the same time. Cooperation allows governments and communities to share information, resources, and experience. In education, schools can organise exchanges and joint research. In the economy, countries can support fair trade and responsible tourism. ASEAN can also promote emergency training and environmental projects. Cooperation does not remove national differences; it helps countries use those differences as strengths. A better regional future depends on trust, practical action, and the active participation of young people.

Hợp tác giúp chính phủ và cộng đồng chia sẻ thông tin, nguồn lực và kinh nghiệm. Trong giáo dục, trường học có thể tổ chức trao đổi và nghiên cứu chung. Trong kinh tế, các nước hỗ trợ thương mại công bằng và du lịch có trách nhiệm. ASEAN cũng có thể thúc đẩy đào tạo ứng phó khẩn cấp và dự án môi trường. Hợp tác không xóa bỏ khác biệt quốc gia mà giúp biến những khác biệt đó thành thế mạnh. Tương lai khu vực tốt đẹp hơn phụ thuộc vào lòng tin, hành động thực tế và sự tham gia tích cực của người trẻ.

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Skills for an ASEAN Student Programme
lessons.topic: Skills for an ASEAN Student Programme
lessons.passage: To qualify for an ASEAN student programme, a student needs more than good marks. Communication skills, teamwork, confidence, and curiosity about current affairs are also important. Participants may have to discuss regional topics, work with international teammates, or live-stream part of an event. They should speak clearly, listen respectfully, and represent their school responsibly. It would be an honour to join such a programme, but participants must be ready to learn rather than simply show what they already know. I am improving my English and presentation skills because I hope to take part in a regional youth activity one day.

Người tham gia có thể phải thảo luận chủ đề khu vực, làm việc với đồng đội quốc tế hoặc phát trực tiếp một phần sự kiện. Các bạn cần nói rõ ràng, lắng nghe tôn trọng và đại diện nhà trường có trách nhiệm. Được tham gia là một niềm vinh dự, nhưng người tham gia phải sẵn sàng học hỏi chứ không chỉ thể hiện điều mình biết. Em đang cải thiện tiếng Anh và kỹ năng thuyết trình để có thể tham gia hoạt động thanh niên khu vực trong tương lai.

lessons.title: Lesson 18: An ASEAN Youth Volunteer Project
lessons.passage: I would like to propose an ASEAN youth volunteer project about clean rivers. Students from several member states could apply for the programme and work with local communities for one week. They would collect waste, interview residents, and design educational activities for children. The project would address an environmental issue while helping participants develop teamwork and leadership skills. Before joining, volunteers should learn basic safety rules and understand local customs. At the end, each team could present a practical proposal for reducing plastic waste. This programme would show that regional cooperation can create visible benefits for both young people and the community.

lessons.title: Lesson 17: The Value of Cultural Exchange
lessons.passage: Cultural exchange allows young people from different ASEAN countries to learn from one another. Participants may share traditional music, food, clothing, festivals, and daily customs. Such experiences can be eye-opening because students discover both differences and similarities across the region. A cultural celebration is not only entertaining; it can also build respect for diversity and reduce stereotypes. During an exchange, students should ask polite questions and avoid judging unfamiliar traditions. In my opinion, cultural exchange helps ASEAN become more than a political or economic organisation. It creates real friendships among people and strengthens the feeling of belonging to one regional community.

Một lễ hội văn hóa không chỉ mang tính giải trí mà còn xây dựng sự tôn trọng đa dạng và giảm định kiến. Trong chương trình trao đổi, học sinh nên đặt câu hỏi lịch sự và tránh phán xét truyền thống chưa quen thuộc. Theo em, trao đổi văn hóa giúp ASEAN không chỉ là tổ chức chính trị hay kinh tế mà còn tạo tình bạn thật sự và củng cố cảm giác thuộc về một cộng đồng khu vực.

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Challenges of Future Cities
lessons.passage: An article about future cities often describes exciting technology, but real cities will still face serious challenges. Rapid population growth may make neighbourhoods overcrowded and create a housing shortage. Old infrastructure may not provide enough water, transport, or waste treatment. Pollution and unequal access to services can also reduce people's quality of life. Therefore, urban development must be sustainable. City leaders should plan affordable housing, protect green areas, upgrade public systems, and involve local communities in decisions. A city is truly modern not when it has the newest devices, but when every resident can live with dignity and opportunity.

Dân số tăng nhanh có thể khiến khu dân cư quá đông và gây thiếu nhà ở. Cơ sở hạ tầng cũ có thể không cung cấp đủ nước, giao thông hoặc xử lý rác thải. Ô nhiễm và sự bất bình đẳng trong tiếp cận dịch vụ cũng làm giảm chất lượng sống. Vì vậy, phát triển đô thị phải bền vững. Lãnh đạo thành phố nên quy hoạch nhà ở vừa túi tiền, bảo vệ khu xanh, nâng cấp hệ thống công cộng và để cộng đồng tham gia quyết định. Thành phố thực sự hiện đại là nơi mọi cư dân được sống có phẩm giá và cơ hội.

Camera không nên xâm phạm quyền riêng tư, và thông tin cá nhân phải được bảo vệ khỏi việc sử dụng sai mục đích. Người dân cần biết dữ liệu nào được thu thập và vì sao. lessons.title: Lesson 13: Future Homes and Buildings
lessons.passage: As the urban population grows, many people may live in high-rise buildings. Future homes should be energy-efficient and comfortable rather than simply tall. Solar panels can produce clean electricity, while smart windows and natural ventilation can reduce energy use. Roof gardens and shared green spaces will give residents places to relax and grow vegetables. Buildings should also collect rainwater and separate waste for recycling. Good design must include safe lifts, public areas, and access for people with disabilities. In my view, future housing should save space without making residents feel isolated from nature or from their neighbours.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Green Transport
lessons.passage: Transport is one of the biggest challenges in modern cities. Traffic jams waste time, create noise, and increase carbon emissions. Future cities should develop reliable public transport and encourage people to use electric vehicles. Safe cycle paths and wide pedestrian zones can make walking and cycling more attractive. Schools and workplaces can provide bicycle parking, while buses and metro systems should be clean, affordable, and punctual. Green transport is not only an environmental solution. It also improves public health because people become more active and breathe cleaner air. A successful city gives citizens convenient alternatives to private cars.

Thành phố tương lai nên phát triển giao thông công cộng đáng tin cậy và khuyến khích sử dụng xe điện.
